docs.title: Documentation style guide
docs.text: These docs are for customers using GoodBards — marketers, not engineers. Everything below exists to keep 40+ pages sounding like one person wrote them.

docs.title: Who you are writing for
docs.text:
A marketing manager at an agency or mid-market company. They are smart, busy, and not technical. They want to finish a task, not understand the system.

  • Write you, not "the user".
  • Use the words the UI uses. If the button says Launch a Tactic, never call it "initiating a tactic workflow".
  • No internal vocabulary: no tenant, sub-tenant, UID, endpoint, connector config, asset entity. Say your company, account, link.
  • Cut every sentence that does not help them finish the task.

docs.title: Page shape
docs.text:
Every feature page follows the same four headings, in this order:

Heading What goes in it What it's for 2–3 sentences on the problem it solves. Before you start Prerequisites. Delete the section if there are none. How to Numbered steps matching the UI exactly. Good to know Limits, gotchas, and mistakes people actually make.

Readers navigate by pattern. Do not invent new section names.

docs.title: Writing steps
docs.text:
• One action per numbered step.
  • Bold every UI label exactly as it appears: choose Save, not click save.
  • Say where things are: "In the sidebar, choose Audience → Contacts."
  • Stop at the outcome: "Your contacts appear in the list."

docs.title: Screenshots
docs.text:
Screenshots carry more weight than prose for this audience, so they must look consistent. The agreed convention:

Setting Value Tenant Demo tenant only. Never real customer data — this site is public. Theme Light Viewport 1440 × 900 Format PNG, saved to docs/img/screenshots/<page-name>.png

Rules:

  • Never screenshot a real customer's account. Names, email addresses, company names and metrics from a live tenant must not appear. PDPA applies.
  • Screen pages: one screenshot unless a step is genuinely unclear without a second. Guides: one per stage is fine, placed right under the step it shows.
  • Capture the relevant panel, not the whole desktop. Crop out the top bar: it shows the signed-in person's name and photo.
  • Always write real alt text: ![The Contacts list with a segment applied](...). Screen-reader users and broken-image fallbacks both depend on it.
  • Re-capture when the UI changes. A stale screenshot is worse than none.
  • Every screenshot opens full size when clicked (glightbox). To opt one out, add { .no-lightbox } after it.

docs.title: Animated GIFs
docs.text:
Use a GIF only when the movement is the instruction: dragging, an editor interaction, a sequence a still image cannot show (for example inserting a field in the email editor). Everything else stays a PNG.

  • Same rules as screenshots: demo tenant, light theme, the panel only.
  • Short: one action, under 10 seconds, no idle frames at the start or end.
  • Under 2 MB. Save to docs/img/gifs/<page-name>-<action>.gif.
  • Alt text says what happens: ![Choosing Attendee name from Insert field…](...).

docs.title: Admonitions
docs.text:
Use them sparingly — one per page at most.

!!! tip "Save time"
    Duplicate last month's campaign instead of starting over.

!!! warning "This cannot be undone"
    Deleting a segment does not delete its contacts, but the segment is gone.

docs.title: Before you commit
docs.text:
Run the build locally and make sure it is clean:

pip install -r requirements.txt
mkdocs serve          # preview at http://127.0.0.1:8000
mkdocs build --strict # fails on broken links

--strict is what CI should eventually enforce. Do not add a page to nav: in mkdocs.yml until the file exists, or the build breaks.

docs.title: Publishing
docs.text: Pushing to main builds and publishes to https://docs.goodbards.ai/ automatically. It takes about a minute. If your change is not live after that, check the Actions tab before assuming DNS.

docs.title: Before you get in touch
docs.text:
Many questions are already answered here:

  • FAQs — the questions we are asked most often.
  • What is GoodBards? — how the platform fits together.
  • Finding Your Way Around — where each feature lives.

If a screen looks different from the documentation, the product may have moved on ahead of these pages — tell us and we will update them.

docs.title: How to reach us
docs.text: Email support@goodbards.com Live chat Bottom right of the app Billing billing@goodbards.com

docs.title: What to include
docs.text:
The more of this you can give us, the faster we can help:

  • What you were trying to do, and what happened instead.
  • The page you were on — the address from your browser is ideal.
  • Your workspace name, shown at the top of the app.
  • A screenshot, if something looks wrong on screen.

Never send us your password

GoodBards support will never ask for your password. If you receive a message claiming to be from us and asking for it, do not reply — forward it to support@goodbards.com.

docs.title: Billing and subscriptions
docs.text:
For invoices, refunds and plan changes, email billing@goodbards.com from the address your account is registered to, and include your workspace name.

To check what your team has used against your plan, see Usage & Billing.

docs.title: How do I reset my password?
docs.text: Go to the login page and choose Forgot Password?. You will receive an email with a reset link.

docs.title: How do I change my name, language or profile picture?
docs.text: In Personal Settings, reached from your profile picture at the top right. See Personal Settings.

docs.title: Can I turn on two-factor authentication?
docs.text: Yes — under Personal Settings → Password & Security. Worth doing: a marketing account can usually email your entire contact database.

docs.title: Why can I not see a section other people mention?
docs.text: What appears in your sidebar depends on your plan and your permissions. Agentic AI in particular is not included in every plan.

docs.title: What should I set up first?
docs.text: Brand & Context, then your Brand Kit, then Connections, then contacts. See Sign Up & Onboarding for why that order.

docs.title: Why is there no data on my analytics pages?
docs.text: Almost always a missing connector. Check Connections — pages such as Google Analytics and Google Trends read from your own accounts and show nothing until those are linked.

docs.title: Some pages take a while to load. Is that normal?
docs.text: Yes. Screens that pull live data from Google can take several seconds. An empty chart usually means it is still loading rather than that there is no data.

docs.title: Does the AI know about my business?
docs.text: It knows what you tell it in Brand & Context — what your company does, how it sounds, who it competes with. Filling that in properly is the single biggest improvement you can make to AI output.

docs.title: Can I control what the AI can see?
docs.text: Yes. Each field in Brand & Context has a Visible to AI / Hide From AI toggle, so you can keep commercially sensitive details out of generated content.

docs.title: Which AI model is used?
docs.text: Set per generation type — text, image, video and audio — in AI Settings. The defaults work well; change them only if you have a specific reason.

docs.title: Does generating content cost anything?
docs.text: It consumes credits from your monthly allowance. Video costs more than images, which cost more than text. Track it in Usage & Billing.

docs.title: What is the difference between a tactic and a campaign?
docs.text: A tactic is one piece of marketing on one channel — a single post, one email. A campaign groups several tactics towards one goal over a period of time. If you just want to publish one post, you want a tactic. See Launch a Tactic.

docs.title: Why is my ad campaign not spending anything?
docs.text: New campaigns start paused, and need at least one enabled ad. See Digital Ads.

docs.title: Can I recall an email after sending it?
docs.text: No. Check your recipient list and send yourself a test first — see Emails.

docs.title: What happens if someone unsubscribes?
docs.text: They move to the unsubscribed group and stop receiving marketing email. Do not work around this by re-importing them — under Singapore's PDPA and equivalent rules elsewhere, opt-outs must be respected.

docs.title: What is the difference between a segment and a mailing list?
docs.text: A segment is a saved rule, re-evaluated each time you use it, so it stays current. A mailing list is a fixed set of contacts. See Contacts.

docs.title: Can I keep separate workspaces for different clients?
docs.text:
Yes, if your plan includes sub-workspaces. Each has its own contacts, campaigns and credit allowance. See Sub-Workspaces.

Not answered here? Contact support.

docs.title: Digital Ads
docs.text:
Plan paid search and follow what your ads bring. In the app, Digital Ads sits under Marketing in the sidebar.

Who sees it: everyone your administrator gives the Digital ads access to.

docs.title: Digital Ads
docs.text:
Your ad campaigns and their results, next to the rest of your marketing.

See Digital Ads.

docs.title: Keyword planner
docs.text:
Research the keywords your market searches for, with volumes and costs, when your Google Ads account is connected.

See Choosing keywords.

docs.title: Agentic AI
docs.text:
AI assistants that do marketing work for you — writing, researching, generating images and audio.

Who sees it: everyone your administrator gives the AI studio access to.

docs.title: In this section
docs.text:
• Chat Agents — assistants you hold a conversation with, each set up for a particular kind of work.
  • Workflow Agents — agents that carry out a multi-step task on your behalf.
  • Research Assistant — ask for research on a market, competitor or topic.
  • Image Generation — create images from a description.
  • Video Generation — create short video clips.
  • Text to Speech — turn written copy into spoken audio.
  • Agent Parameters — the variables your agents' prompts can use, such as Audience, CallToAction or Boilerplate100. Many are filled in for you from your Brand & Context, such as your company boilerplate. The colour of each row shows whether it is a global, system or local variable; New Variable adds your own. Most teams never need to change them.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text: Agentic AI is not included in every plan. If this section does not appear in your sidebar, your plan does not include agents.

docs.title: Chat Agents
docs.text: Assistants you can hold a conversation with — each one set up for a particular kind of marketing work.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
A chat agent is an AI assistant you talk to in plain language. Rather than one general-purpose chatbot, GoodBards gives you several, each pointed at a different job: one that understands your brand narrative, one that reads your contact data, one that looks after retention.

Agents know your business. They can draw on your Brand Kit and, depending on the tools they are given, on your campaigns, contacts and analytics.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: Chat agents are not available on every plan. If Agentic AI does not appear in your sidebar, your plan does not include agents — speak to your account contact.

docs.title: How to start a chat
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, choose Agentic AI → Chat Agents.
  2. Browse the agents, or use Search agents… to find one by name.
  3. Choose the agent that fits what you need, and start typing.

docs.title: Reading an agent card
docs.text:
Each card tells you what the agent is and what it can reach:

On the card What it means Global / Local Global agents are provided by GoodBards. Local agents were created inside your own account. Category The kind of work it is for — General, Data Analysis, Content and Post, Research, Chatbot. Description What the agent is designed to do. Features Capabilities switched on for it. Some agents show No feature enabled yet. Tools What it can actually reach — Marketing Campaigns, Google Analytics, Google Trends and so on.

Tools are the part that matters

Two agents with similar descriptions can behave very differently depending on their tools. An agent with Google Analytics in its tool list can answer questions about your traffic; one without it cannot.

docs.title: Filtering by category
docs.text: The buttons under the title narrow the list: All, Content and Post, Data Analysis, General, Research, Chatbot. A greyed-out category has no agents in it.

docs.title: Creating your own
docs.text:
+ Create New Agent builds an agent for your account, which appears as Local. Your plan sets how many custom agents you may have. The Tutorial button at the top walks you through the form.

Part What to set General Information A name, an avatar, the agent type and its category, and a short description your team will see on its card. Prompt Definition The AI model, and the System Prompt: who the agent is and how it should behave. A good starting prompt is already filled in; adapt it to the agent's job. Optional: a User Prompt added to every conversation, a Welcome Message and Sample Requests shown when a chat starts. Data Retrievers Search Knowledge Base: let the agent read your Content Repository files marked for AI. Web Search: let it search the web. Tools The actions the agent may take inside GoodBards, and outside tools connected under AI Settings → MCP Tools. As you pick internal tools, a table under the selector lists what each one lets the agent do: one row per tool, one chip per operation (for example listMarketingCampaigns or createMarketingAsset). Hover a chip to read what the operation does and what it needs. The last rows, marked Always on, are the core abilities every agent has, such as web search and the current date. Agent Skills Ready-made expertise, assigned once the agent exists. Memory Persistent Memory lets the agent remember facts from past conversations; Promote Facts to Tenant shares important ones with all your agents. Leave the numbers at their defaults unless support asks you to change them.

Choose Create Agent. To change an agent later, use the pencil on its card. Global agents, provided by GoodBards, cannot be edited.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Agents are not identical. Pick by tools, not by name.
  • An agent only knows what its tools reach. If it cannot see your contacts, it cannot answer questions about them.
  • Global agents are maintained for you. They may gain capabilities over time without you changing anything.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Image Generation
docs.text: Create images for campaigns, posts and emails by describing what you want.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
Marketing needs images constantly, and stock photography rarely fits. Describe the image you need and GoodBards creates it — no design software, no photo shoot.

Generated images are useful for social posts, email headers and campaign visuals. They are less suited to anything needing your actual products or people.

docs.title: How to generate an image
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, choose Agentic AI → Image Generation.
  2. Describe what you want in Prompt. Detail helps.
  3. Aspect Ratio, Brand and Style Options are folded sections. Each shows its current choice next to its name (for example 1:1 or Tropika Home · Logo stamped). Open one to change it. Your primary brand kit is already selected under Brand (see below).
  4. Choose Generate Images, always at the bottom of the panel.

Your images appear under Generated Images on the left.

docs.title: Keeping images on brand
docs.text:
Brand kit lists your company's brand kits. Your primary kit is selected when you open the screen. Choose None to generate without it.

With a brand kit selected, GoodBards adds the kit's colours and its imagery guidelines to your prompt, so the result leans towards your palette and style. AI follows colours closely but not exactly, so check important brand colours by eye.

docs.title: Adding your logo
docs.text:
Turn on Add logo to place your real logo on the image:

  • Logo: pick which of the kit's logos to use. GoodBards remembers your choice for that kit.
  • Variant: Auto picks the white version on dark backgrounds and the normal one on light backgrounds. You can also pick a version yourself.
  • Position and Size: choose the corner and how large the logo is.

The logo is your actual logo file placed on top of the image. The AI never redraws it, so it is never distorted. Changing the logo, position or size updates the image instantly and uses no credits. Download, Edit and Save to Drive all keep the logo.

Brand rules about logo placement

If your brand kit says the logo belongs top-left, Position starts there.

docs.title: Putting your logo inside the scene
docs.text:
With a Nano Banana or GPT Image model, you can also turn on Blend logo into the scene. The AI then draws your logo into the picture itself: printed on a cup, a bag, a shop sign. Pick the logo and variant as above.

The AI redraws the logo, so it may not reproduce it perfectly. Check its shape, colours and lettering before you use the image. For an exact logo, use Add logo instead. You can only use one of the two at a time.

The same Brand kit choice appears when you generate an image for a campaign tactic. That screen adds your colours and guidelines, but not the logo.

docs.title: Choosing an aspect ratio
docs.text:
Ratio Shape Good for 1024x1024 Square Instagram posts, profile images. 1536x1024 Landscape Email headers, website banners, LinkedIn. 1024x1536 Portrait Stories, vertical mobile formats. auto Chosen for you When you are not sure.

Pick the ratio for where the image will be used. Cropping a square image into a banner afterwards usually spoils the composition.

docs.title: Writing a good prompt
docs.text:
Be specific about subject, setting, style and mood. "A flat-lay of tropical fruit on a pale marble table, bright daylight, minimal styling" gives a far better result than "fruit picture".

AI Assist writes the prompt for you

AI Assist, above the prompt box, expands a rough idea into a fuller description. Useful when you know what you want but not how to describe it.

docs.title: Choosing a model
docs.text: Model at the top sets which AI generates the image. The default comes from your company's AI Settings; change it here to use a different one for this image.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Generation uses credits. Each image counts against your allowance — see Usage & Billing.
  • Expect to iterate. The first result is rarely the one you use. Adjust the prompt and generate again.
  • Check faces, hands and text. AI images still get these wrong, and mistakes are more obvious to your audience than to you.
  • Do not generate real people or brands. Images resembling identifiable people or another company's branding carry legal risk.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Research Assistant
docs.text: Ask a question about a market, competitor or topic, and get a researched answer back.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
Some questions need more than a quick answer — what are the main loyalty programmes among Singapore F&B chains, and how do they differ? The Research Assistant works through questions like that properly rather than replying off the top of its head.

Use it for market scans, competitor comparisons and background before a campaign. For quick drafting, a chat agent is faster.

docs.title: How to request research
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, choose Agentic AI → Research Assistant.
  2. Type your question in the box at the bottom.
  3. Send it, and wait — this takes longer than an ordinary chat reply.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The assistant takes four steps, which is why it is slower and better than a single answer:

Stage What happens Ask Your Question You describe what you want to know. Be specific. Break It Down Your question is split into smaller subtopics to explore from several angles. Research in Depth Each subtopic is examined and the findings pulled together. Get Your Results You get a fuller, more rounded answer than a quick reply would give.

Specific questions get better research

"Tell me about coffee" produces something bland. "How do specialty coffee brands in Singapore position themselves against chains, and what do they charge?" gives the assistant something to work with.

docs.title: Chat History
docs.text: Chat History, at the top right, holds your previous research. Worth checking before asking again — someone may already have researched the same ground.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Responses take a while. The screen says so, and that is the trade-off for depth. Ask, then come back to it.
  • Research costs credits. More than a simple chat, because it runs several searches. See Usage & Billing.
  • Verify anything load-bearing. Check facts you plan to publish — prices, statistics and competitor claims especially.
  • It is a starting point. Use the research to inform your own judgement, not to replace it.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Text to Speech
docs.text: Turn written copy into spoken audio, in a voice you choose.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
Some audiences listen rather than read. Text to Speech produces audio from your written copy — useful for video voiceovers, social clips, accessible versions of written content, and audio ads.

You write the script; the platform reads it aloud.

docs.title: How to generate audio
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, choose Agentic AI → Text to Speech.
  2. Paste or type your script into Text. The limit is 5,000 characters.
  3. Pick a Voice.
  4. Choose Generate Audio.

Your audio appears under Audio Preview on the left.

docs.title: Choosing a voice
docs.text:
Each voice has a short description of how it sounds:

Voice Character Kore Warm, female Charon Deep, male Puck Energetic, neutral Fenrir Strong, male Aoede Soft, female Leda Clear, female

Match the voice to the content. Energetic suits a product launch; warm or soft suits something more considered.

Pick one voice and stay with it

If audio becomes a regular part of your marketing, using the same voice each time makes it recognisable. Switching voices between clips sounds like different companies talking.

docs.title: Writing for the ear
docs.text:
Copy that reads well on a page often sounds wrong aloud. Shorter sentences work better, and it is worth reading your script out before generating it.

AI Assist, above the text box, can help adapt written copy into something that sounds natural spoken.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• 5,000 characters is roughly five minutes. Longer scripts need splitting.
  • Listen before you publish. Check names, acronyms and any local place names — these are where pronunciation goes wrong.
  • Generation uses credits. See Usage & Billing.
  • Say if audio is synthetic where your audience would reasonably expect a real person.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Video Generation
docs.text: Create short video clips from a written description.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
Short video performs well on social, and producing it normally means a camera, an editor and a week. This generates a clip from a description instead — useful for social posts, ad creative and background footage.

Clips are short by design: a few seconds, suited to social rather than long-form storytelling.

docs.title: How to generate a video
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, choose Agentic AI → Video Generation.
  2. Describe the clip you want in Prompt.
  3. Starting Image, Aspect Ratio, Duration, Brand and Style Options are folded sections. Each shows its current choice next to its name (for example 16:9 or 8s). Open one to change it. Your primary brand kit is already selected under Brand.
  4. Choose Generate Video, always at the bottom of the panel.

Your clip appears under Video Preview on the left.

docs.title: Aspect ratio
docs.text:
Ratio Use it for 16:9 Landscape YouTube, website embeds, presentations. 9:16 Portrait Stories, Reels, TikTok — anything watched on a phone held upright.

Choose before generating. Cropping landscape footage into portrait afterwards cuts the sides off your subject.

docs.title: Duration
docs.text: Clips run from 5s to 8s. Shorter is usually better on social, where the first two seconds decide whether anyone keeps watching.

docs.title: Starting from an image
docs.text:
Under Starting Image, choose Upload or From Drive. The video starts from that picture and brings it to life. GoodBards switches the aspect ratio to the one closest to your picture.

This is how you get your logo into the scene, for example on a flag, a shop sign or a product. Video models never see your logo file, so a prompt like "use our logo" on its own produces a video without it.

  1. In Image Generation, create the opening shot with Blend logo into the scene on. Use the aspect ratio you want for the video. Keep the version where the logo looks best, and choose Save to Drive.
  2. In Video Generation, open Starting Image, choose From Drive and pick that image.
  3. In the prompt, describe the motion and the camera. Say that the emblem is already correct and must stay identical. Don't ask for an uploaded logo.

The logo can drift

The AI redraws every frame from the first one. With a lot of motion, your logo can lose detail as the clip goes on. Calmer camera moves keep it sharper. Watch the whole clip before you publish it.

docs.title: Keeping videos on brand
docs.text:
Brand lists your company's brand kits. With a kit selected, GoodBards adds its colours and imagery guidelines to your prompt. Choose None to generate without it.

Turn on Add logo to stamp your real logo file in a corner, as in Image Generation: pick the logo, the variant, the position and the size. The preview shows it straight away. Download and Save to Drive then record the clip again with the logo on every frame. This takes as long as the clip itself, so keep the tab open. You get an MP4 in Chrome, Edge and Brave, and a WebM file in some other browsers.

docs.title: Style options
docs.text: Style, Lighting, Mood, Camera / Angle and Color Palette add a look to your prompt without you having to write it, for example Photorealistic with Golden Hour lighting. They are the same options as in Image Generation. Leave them on Any to rely on the prompt alone, or choose Reset Style Options to clear them.

docs.title: Writing a good prompt
docs.text:
Describe the shot the way you would brief a videographer — subject, movement, setting, light. The placeholder on screen is a good model: a cinematic drone shot flying over misty mountains at sunrise.

AI Assist above the prompt box expands a rough idea into a fuller description.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Video costs more than images. Generation is slower and uses more credits — see Usage & Billing.
  • Expect several attempts. Getting the motion right usually takes a few tries, so allow time before a deadline.
  • Watch for artefacts. Faces, hands and text are where AI video still fails. Watch the clip fully before publishing.
  • Add captions. Most social video is watched with the sound off.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Workflow Agents
docs.text: Multi-step jobs that run themselves — research, analysis and planning that would take you an afternoon.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
A chat agent answers a question. A workflow agent carries out a whole process: researching a company, comparing it with competitors, ranking them, and producing a SWOT analysis — each step feeding the next.

You start it and come back to the result.

docs.title: How to run a workflow
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, choose Agentic AI → Workflow Agents.
  2. Browse the workflows, or filter by category.
  3. Read the diagram to see what it will do.
  4. Choose Start Workflow.

docs.title: Reading the diagram
docs.text:
Each workflow shows its steps as a flow chart, so you can see what happens before you start it. A company research workflow, for example, runs:

Start → Company Research → Competition Analysis → Competition Ranking → SWOT Analysis

Some workflows fan out and rejoin — splitting a question into parts, working on each separately, then merging the findings. That is why they take longer than a single answer and produce a more thorough one.

Read the diagram first

The flow chart tells you what the agent will actually do. If the steps do not match what you need, a different workflow — or a chat agent — may suit you better.

docs.title: Categories
docs.text:
Filter with the buttons under the title: All, Campaign and Execution, Operational, Strategy and Planning, Tactics. A greyed-out category has no workflows in it.

Use Search agents… to find one by name.

docs.title: Chat History
docs.text: Chat History on each workflow holds previous runs. Worth checking before starting a fresh one — a colleague may have run the same analysis last month.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Results are not instant. These run several steps in sequence; expect to come back to them.
  • Workflows use more credits than a chat. Each step costs. See Usage & Billing.
  • Check the output before acting on it. A workflow producing competitor analysis is a starting point for your judgement, not a decision.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Audience
docs.text:
Everyone you market to: the people, the organisations they work for, and how they engage with you.

Who sees it: everyone your administrator gives the Audience access to. Depending on their role, a colleague may see only the contacts they own.

docs.title: Contacts
docs.text:
The people you market to, with their details, custom fields, status and history of every email, form and event. Group them into segments that update themselves as contacts change.

See Contacts.

docs.title: Companies
docs.text:
The organisations your contacts belong to, with their own segments.

See Companies.

docs.title: Mailing lists
docs.text:
Lists people subscribe to, for example from a sign-up form. A contact who unsubscribes stays unsubscribed: adding them again by hand does not override their choice.

See Mailing lists.

docs.title: Adding contacts
docs.text:
Add one contact, import a spreadsheet with Bulk Add Contacts, or photograph a business card with Scan Business Card. Import Jobs shows how each import went.

See Adding contacts.

docs.title: Lead scoring
docs.text:
A 0–100 score per contact, from what they did: opened, clicked, registered, attended. Use it to see who is ready for a sales conversation.

See Lead scoring.

docs.title: Why this comes first
docs.text: Almost everything else depends on your audience. Emails need recipients, forms create contacts, and reporting is only as good as the data behind it. If you are setting up GoodBards for the first time, get contacts in before building campaigns.

docs.title: Adding contacts
docs.text: Bring people into your audience: one at a time, from a spreadsheet, or from a business card.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text: Most contacts arrive on their own, from your forms, events and chatbot. The rest you add yourself: the list from a trade show, a client's customer file, the cards you collected at a meeting. Each way below creates proper contacts, with their consent and where they came from recorded.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• The Access sensitive data permission. Without it, Add Contact and Bulk Add Contacts are greyed out. Importing also requires being an administrator. Ask an administrator to give it to you under Tenant Settings → Security; see Additional permissions.
  • Your company's privacy statement, under Brand & Context → General Information → Privacy Statements. Every import is linked to the statement the people agreed to.

docs.title: Add one contact
docs.text: In Audience → Contacts, on the Details List tab, choose Add Contact and fill in the form.

docs.title: Import a spreadsheet
docs.text:
1. In Audience → Contacts, open the Import Jobs tab, then Bulk Add Contacts → From a CSV file.
  2. Choose Download Template and put your contacts in it, one per row. The columns and the values they accept are explained in Contacts → Prepare your CSV file.

  3. Upload the file, give the import a Title, and choose:

    • Choose Conflict Action: what to do when an email address already exists (for example Ignore it).
    • Default Status: the status of the imported contacts.

  4. Under Additional Details, say where the contacts come from (a campaign and tactic, or another source), add Tags and Owners, and pick the Privacy Statement they agreed to. Choose Upload.

  5. The job appears on the Import Jobs tab as READY TO START. Nothing is imported yet: check the job, then choose Start and confirm with Start import.
  6. When the job shows COMPLETED, your contacts are in. If it shows INCOMPLETE, open it with View and choose Download logs to see which rows were rejected and why. See Import Jobs.

docs.title: Import from Pipedrive
docs.text: Once Pipedrive is connected (see Pipedrive), Bulk Add Contacts → From Pipedrive imports your Pipedrive contacts directly, with the same choices as a spreadsheet: conflict action, default status, tags and privacy statement. Until Pipedrive is connected, the option shows as Not connected.

docs.title: Scan a business card
docs.text:
1. In Audience → Contacts, open the Card Scanner tab.
  2. Choose Take Photo, or Choose File for a picture you already have.
  3. GoodBards reads the card and fills in the Contact Information. Check it, correct anything misread, and save.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Only import people who agreed to hear from you. Set the Default Status to match what they agreed to: choose Subscribed only for people who gave marketing consent. Under Singapore's PDPA and similar laws, consent cannot be assumed.
  • The conflict action handles existing contacts. It decides what happens to a row whose contact is already in your audience.
  • Tag every import. A tag such as trade-show-2026 lets you find, segment and follow up that group later.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Companies
docs.text: The organisations your contacts work for — and how complete your picture of them is.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
In B2B marketing the company matters as much as the person. Several contacts may work at the same organisation, and a decision usually involves more than one of them.

Companies group your contacts by the organisation they belong to, so you can see account-level activity rather than isolated individuals.

docs.title: Reading the Companies home
docs.text:
Audience → Companies opens on Home, which summarises your data rather than listing organisations.

Total Companies, top left, shows how many organisations you hold.

Data quality, next to it, is your clean-up list for accounts. Each tile counts the companies that need attention, with their share of the total; hover it to read what it checks, and choose it to open the list filtered to those companies:

  • No contacts — organisations nobody at your company can reach. Add or link a contact.
  • Under 5 contacts — accounts below the number of contacts you aim for. On the filtered list, change the number in the filter chip above the table to use your own target.

In the Details List, the Contacts column shows how many contacts each company has; sort on it to see the thinnest accounts first. The assistant in the top bar answers the same questions in plain words, for example companies with fewer than 5 contacts or top 10 companies by clicks in the last 30 days; see Asking the assistant.

docs.title: Database Health
docs.text:
The charts below score how complete your data is:

  • Company Database Count — how it has grown.
  • Database Growth — the rate of growth.
  • Field Completeness — the percentage of fields filled in. Low completeness limits how well you can segment.
  • Distribution by Industry — which sectors you hold. Companies with no industry set show as Unknown.
  • Distribution by Company Size — the spread from small to large.

The letter badge beside Database Health grades your data overall, and the small line next to it shows the score over the last 90 days. Treat a low grade as a prompt to fill in missing fields rather than a problem with the platform. Engagement, further down, grades how much your accounts interact with you.

docs.title: Adding companies
docs.text: On the Details List tab, choose Add Company. Link contacts to it from the company field of each contact.

docs.title: A company's page
docs.text:
Choose a company's code in the Details List to open its page.

Section What it shows About and Company Details The description, code, annual revenue, employees and timezone. Location Country, city and address. Custom Fields Your own company fields, such as a gifting budget. Timeline Owners, and when the record was created and last updated. Social Links and Legal Information Social profiles, registration number and legal entity type. Contact List The people who work there, with their status, and which one is marked as the main recipient.

Choose Edit Company to change the details.

docs.title: The other tabs
docs.text: Tab What it holds Details List All your companies, with owners; assign owners in bulk with Assign Owners. Segments Saved filters over companies, for example hotels in Singapore. Custom Fields Your own company fields. Same as for contacts: see Custom Fields. Custom Lists The value lists for Select fields. See Custom Lists.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Unknown industry limits targeting. You cannot segment by a field you have not filled in.
  • Link contacts to companies. An unlinked contact cannot be counted towards the account they work for.
  • Nominate a main contact. It is who the platform treats as your route into that organisation.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Contacts
docs.text: The people you market to — how to add them, keep their details current, and group them into segments.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text: Every email you send and every form someone fills in comes back to a contact. Contacts are the centre of the platform: get them right and the rest of your marketing has something to work with.

docs.title: Adding contacts
docs.text:
There is more than one way, depending on how many you have:

Method Use it when Add one at a time You met someone and want them in straight away. Import You have a list to bring across. Progress shows under Import Jobs. Card Scanner You came back from an event with a stack of business cards. Scan them and the details are read for you. Forms Someone signs up themselves. See Forms.

Adding and importing need the Access sensitive data permission

A contact is mostly an email address and a phone number, so only colleagues allowed to see them can add or import contacts. Without the Access sensitive data permission, Add Contact and Bulk Add Contacts are greyed out; hover them to see why. Importing also requires being an administrator. See Additional permissions.

docs.title: Reading the Contacts home
docs.text:
Audience → Contacts opens on the Home tab, which summarises your database rather than listing individuals.

Total Contacts, top left, shows how many contacts you hold. The gauge fills as you approach your plan's limit and turns orange, then red, near it. On a plan without a limit, it shows the number alone.

The Status distribution card, under Database Health, shows how those contacts split between statuses:

  • Subscribed — contacts who have agreed to hear from you.
  • Regular — contacts with no marketing consent yet: you can work with them, but not email them marketing.
  • Unsubscribed, Bounced and Do not contact — people you must not email.

Subscribed is the number that matters

A large database is not much use if most of it has unsubscribed. Only Subscribed contacts can receive marketing email.

Bounced and Do not contact are set for you

When a marketing email cannot be delivered, GoodBards reads the reply from the recipient's mail server. An address that does not exist, or whose server rejects the message outright, becomes Bounced at once. A temporary problem (full mailbox, message too large, content refused) only adds a note to the contact; after three sends that bounce this way, the contact becomes Bounced too. A recipient who reports your email as spam becomes Do not contact. Both statuses stop every further send, and the reason stays in the contact's engagement timeline and notes.

Data quality, next to it, is your clean-up list. Each tile counts the contacts that need attention, with their share of your database. Hover a tile to read exactly what it checks:

  • No company — people you cannot count towards an account.
  • Missing info — contacts missing an email, phone or country: records you cannot reach or segment. Email and phone are only checked when your role can see them.
  • No owner — nobody is responsible for them.
  • Possible duplicates — pairs of records with the same first and last name. Review them before merging anything.

Choose a tile to open the list filtered to exactly those rows; a chip above the table shows the filter and the count, with a cross to clear it. A tile with nothing to fix shows All good.

docs.title: The grades
docs.text:
Database Health grades how usable your database is, and Engagement how much your contacts interact with you. Each is a score out of 100 shown as a letter: A (90–100), B (75–89), C (60–74), D (40–59) or F (below 40). Choose the grade to see its formula.

Beside each grade, a small line shows the score over the last 90 days, with how many points it gained or lost. Hover the line to read the score on a given day. It builds up day by day.

Why the Database Health line can jump

Part of the score compares this month's new contacts with last month's. On the first days of a month the comparison starts again, so the line can drop even though nothing got worse. The score also steps up as your database passes 100, 500, 1,000 and 10,000 contacts.

Grade Made of Database Health Profile completeness (50 points): how many contacts have a first and last name, company, job title, country, preferred language and phone. Volume (25 points): how many contacts you hold. Growth momentum (25 points): new contacts this month against last month. Engagement Engaged share (50 points): contacts with a score of 40 or more. Reach (25 points): contacts with any engagement at all. Depth (25 points): the average score per contact.

To raise database health, fill in the missing details (an import with the Overwrite conflict action can complete existing contacts). To raise engagement, send your contacts something worth opening. See Lead scoring.

Companies have the same two grades, built from company data. See Companies.

docs.title: Finding individual contacts
docs.text:
The Details List tab lists every contact: their code, name, owner, email, status and last update.

  • Search by name or email, and choose the columns to show with View.
  • The Company column shows the account a contact is linked to (a +1 badge means more than one; hover to see them all). Sort on it to group contacts by company, or to bring the unlinked ones to the top.
  • Each contact can have owners, the colleagues responsible for them. Filter by owner, or select contacts and choose Assign Owners. Depending on their role, a colleague may only see the contacts they own.
  • Export As CSV downloads the list; Add Contact creates one.
  • Click a contact's code to open their record: details, custom fields, mailing lists, and the history of every email, form and event.

docs.title: Asking the assistant
docs.text:
On the Contacts and Companies pages, the assistant in the top bar answers questions about your audience, in plain words:

  • Which contacts have no company?
  • Find Jon Tan from DBS, I am not sure of the spelling.
  • Who opened the last newsletter but never clicked?
  • Who went cold in the last six months?
  • Top 10 companies by clicks in the last 30 days.

It reads the same data as the screens, under the same rules: it only sees the contacts you can see, it never shows an email or phone your role cannot see, and it does not edit anything. When you open a contact's record, "this contact" in your question means that person. Each answer states the rule it applied (for example contacts with no positive engagement in the last 180 days), so you can check it before acting.

docs.title: A contact's page
docs.text:
Choose a contact's code in the list to open their page: everything GoodBards knows about them, in one place.

Section What it shows Scores The engagement score and the decay score next to the name. See Lead scoring. Contact Summary Job, companies, email, phone, customer type, preferred contact method, referral source and owners. Location Country, city, address and timezone. Custom Fields Your own fields, such as a loyalty tier or a home store. Policies The privacy statements the contact accepted, when, and how (for example through a form). This is your proof of consent. Mailing Lists The lists they belong to, how they joined (public sign-up, added manually) and whether they are still subscribed. Events and Form submissions The events they registered for and the forms they filled in. Social Links, Referral Info, Tags Their social profiles, where they came from, and your tags. Engagement Over Time and Engagement Timeline Every open, click, form, registration and subscription, day by day and in order.

docs.title: Editing a contact
docs.text:
Choose Edit Contact at the top right. The form has the personal details, address and timezone, job and companies, subscription status, social handles, referral source, preferred contact method, customer type, privacy statement, mailing lists, tags and Contact Notes. Choose Save Contact when done.

  • Notes keep what your team knows that fits no field: met at the Mid Valley styling clinic. Choose Add Note.
  • Adding a mailing list here subscribes the contact straight away. Only do it for people who agreed.
  • Owners can be changed here by an administrator. See Users, roles & permissions.

docs.title: Segments
docs.text:
A segment is a saved filter — a rule that decides who belongs, evaluated when you use it, so it stays current as contacts change.

To create one, open the Segments tab and choose Add Segment, then set the rule. A segment can filter on contact details (such as country or job title), on behaviour (what contacts did) and on alerts.

Choose a segment's name to open it: its description, its filters, a summary of which kinds of filter are applied, and the list of contacts it holds right now. Edit Segment changes the rule.

Useful segments look like:

  • Singapore members — everyone in one market
  • Corporate buyers — one type of customer
  • Bangkok launch list — the people from one event

Segments beat one-off filters

If you find yourself applying the same filter repeatedly, save it as a segment. Give it a description too — in six months you will not remember what the rule was.

docs.title: Mailing Lists
docs.text: Lists people subscribe to, for example from a sign-up form. See Mailing lists.

docs.title: Card Scanner
docs.text: Photograph a business card, or upload a picture of one: GoodBards reads it and fills in a new contact for you to check and save. See Adding contacts.

docs.title: Custom Fields
docs.text:
The details GoodBards does not hold by default, but your business needs: a loyalty tier, a preferred store, a renewal date.

  1. Open the Custom Fields tab, then create a field.

  2. Give it a Field Name and a Field Type:

    Type Holds Text Free text. Number A number, for example a budget. Date A date, for example a renewal date. Boolean Yes or no. Select A value from a list you define under Custom Lists.

    Tick Allow multiple values when a contact can have several, for example several preferred stores.

  3. Choose whether it applies to Contact, Company or both, under Entity, then Create Field.

The field then appears on every contact's page and in the contact form, and can be shown as a column in the Details List with View.

Deleting a field deletes its values

Removing a custom field removes the values stored in it for every contact. It cannot be undone.

docs.title: Custom Lists
docs.text:
The lists of values used by Select custom fields: statuses, categories, types. Example: a Store list with Jurong Point, Mid Valley and CentralWorld.

  1. Open the Custom Lists tab, then Add Reference List.
  2. Give it a Technical List Identifier (letters, digits, - and _, for example store) and a List Name.
  3. Add the entries with Add Entry, each with a code and a label. Drag them to reorder, or sort them alphabetically.

Write names and labels in English: GoodBards translates them automatically into the other languages of the app.

docs.title: Import Jobs
docs.text: Every spreadsheet import, with its status and how many rows were processed, so you can check that an import went through. Start a new one with Bulk Add Contacts, which requires the Access sensitive data permission and an administrator role. See Adding contacts.

docs.title: An import happens in two steps
docs.text:
Uploading a file does not import anything yet. You first create the job, then you start it:

  1. Create the job. Choose Bulk Add Contacts → From a CSV file, upload your file and fill in the form, then choose Upload. The job appears in the list as READY TO START. No contact has been created or changed.
  2. Start the job. In the job's row, choose Start, then Start import to confirm. GoodBards reads the file row by row and creates or updates the contacts. Once started, an import cannot be stopped.

Until you start it, you can still Delete the job, for example if you picked the wrong file or the wrong Default Status, and create a new one.

docs.title: Job statuses
docs.text:
Status What it means READY TO START The file is uploaded but not imported. Choose Start. COMPLETED Every row was imported. INCOMPLETE The import ran, but some rows were rejected. Open the job with View to see which. FAILED The file could not be read at all, for example because it has no header row.

View opens the job's summary: rows processed, imported and failed, the choices made when it was created, and Download logs, which explains line by line why a row was rejected. Download original file gives back the file you uploaded, so you can fix it and import again.

Deleting a job removes it from the list. The contacts it imported stay.

docs.title: Prepare your CSV file
docs.text:
The easiest start is Download Template in the Bulk Add Contacts form: it holds every column, including one for each of your custom fields, and an example row to replace.

Here is a short example you can copy, or download it:

email,customerCode,firstName,lastName,phone,status,customerType,customerTypeInternal,jobTitle,companyName,city,country,timezone,preferredContactMethod,tags,notes,engagementType,engagementDate
mei.tan@example.com,,Mei,Tan,+6591234567,subscribed,b2b,client-customer,Marketing Manager,Lion City Retail,Singapore,Singapore,Asia/Singapore,email,trade-show-2026;vip,Met at booth 12,event-attended,2026-09-24 14:30
arif.rahman@example.com,CUS00102,Arif,Rahman,+60123456789,regular,b2b,target-potential-customer,Head of Growth,Kopi Digital,Kuala Lumpur,Malaysia,Asia/Kuala_Lumpur,whatsapp,trade-show-2026,,,
linh.nguyen@example.com,,Linh,Nguyen,,,b2c,,,,Ho Chi Minh City,Vietnam,Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh,email,,,,

Linh's status is empty, so she gets the Default Status chosen for the job.

The rules of the file:

  • The first row holds the column names, spelled exactly as below, capitals included (firstName, not First Name). A column whose name is not recognised is treated as a custom field, so a misspelt Email column is not read as the email address.
  • A custom field column is named after the field's key (interest_category, not Interest category). For a field that allows multiple values, separate them with semicolons, as for tags: Fitness;Nutrition.
  • Keep only the columns you need, in any order. Every row must have as many cells as the header row, even when they are empty.
  • Separate cells with commas, and put a cell in double quotes if it contains a comma: "Tan, Mei".
  • Save as UTF-8. In Excel, choose CSV UTF-8 (Comma delimited), so that accents and Chinese, Thai or Vietnamese characters come through.
  • Codes are written in lower case, exactly as listed below: subscribed, not Subscribed.

docs.title: The columns
docs.text: Column What to put in it email The contact's email address. This is how GoodBards recognises a contact who is already in your audience. customerCode Your own reference for the contact, for example from your CRM. Must be unique. Left empty, the email address is used. A row needs at least an email or a customerCode. firstName, lastName The contact's name. birthDate Date of birth, as YYYY-MM-DD: 1982-03-03. secondaryEmail, phone, secondaryPhone Other ways to reach them. Write phone numbers with the country code: +6591234567. status Whether you may email them. See Accepted values. customerType b2b (a business contact) or b2c (a consumer). customerTypeInternal Your relationship with them. See Accepted values. timezone Their time zone, as a city name: Asia/Singapore, Asia/Jakarta, Asia/Bangkok. jobTitle Their job title. companyCode, companyName Their company. A company that does not exist yet is created and linked to the contact. street, city, state, country, zipCode Their address. linkedin, facebook, twitter, instagram Their social media profiles. preferredContactMethod How they prefer to be contacted. See Accepted values. tags Tags for this contact, separated by a semicolon: trade-show-2026;vip. notes Free text, added as a note on the contact. engagementType, engagementDate Something the contact did, to record in their history. Fill in both or neither. The date is YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM: 2026-09-24 14:30. See Accepted values. your custom fields One column per custom field, named as in Download Template.

docs.title: Accepted values
docs.text:
The columns below only accept the codes listed. A row with any other value is rejected, and the job ends as INCOMPLETE. An empty cell is always accepted.

status: whether you may send them marketing email.

Code Shown as Meaning subscribed Subscribed They agreed to receive your marketing emails. Only Subscribed contacts are emailed. regular Regular No marketing consent yet. You can work with them, but not email them marketing. unsubscribed Unsubscribed They opted out. do-not-contact Do not contact They must not be contacted at all. invalid-email Bounced Their address does not work. GoodBards usually sets this itself when an email bounces.

Left empty, a new contact gets the Default Status you chose for the job.

customerTypeInternal: your relationship with the contact.

Code Shown as target-potential-customer Target (Potential Customer) client-customer Client/Customer partner Partner strategic-alliance Strategic Alliance technology-partner Technology Partner reseller-channel-partner Reseller/Channel Partner distributor Distributor supplier-vendor Supplier/Vendor competitor Competitor

customerType: b2b or b2c.

preferredContactMethod: email, phone-call, sms-text-message, whatsapp, facebook-messenger, push-notifications, direct-mail, in-person-visit or do-not-contact.

engagementType: the most useful for an import are event-registered, event-attended, form-filled and list-subscribe. Email engagements (email-sent, email-delivered, email-opened, email-clicked, email-unsubscribe) are also accepted, for history brought over from another tool.

docs.title: When a contact already exists
docs.text:
A row whose email is already in your audience is handled by the job's Choose Conflict Action:

  • Ignore: the contact's details are kept as they are. The row's notes are still added, and the contact still receives the job's tags, source and privacy statement.
  • Overwrite: every cell you filled in replaces the contact's current value. Empty cells leave the current value unchanged, so an import never erases data.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Segments update themselves; mailing lists do not. A segment re-evaluates its rule each time; a mailing list stays as you built it.
  • Watch your plan limit. The Total Contacts gauge shows how close you are.
  • Respect unsubscribes. Under Singapore's PDPA and equivalent rules elsewhere, contacts who opt out must not receive marketing email. GoodBards excludes them, but do not work around it by re-importing them.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Lead scoring
docs.text: A score per contact, from what they actually did: opened, clicked, registered, came to your event. Use it to see who is ready for a conversation.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text: A list of 3,000 contacts does not tell you who to call first. The score does. Every engagement adds points, the strongest signals add the most, and points fade over time, so the people at the top are the ones engaging now.

docs.title: Where you see it
docs.text:
Open a contact in Audience → Contacts. Next to their name:

  • Engagement Score: all the points they have earned.
  • Decay Score: the same points, faded with time. Recent activity counts fully, older activity less.

The contact's Engagement Distribution shows where the points come from.

docs.title: How points are earned
docs.text:
Points follow one ladder: about 100 points is a guest who registered for an event and came. Everything else is measured against that.

Signal Effect on the score Opening an email A few points, once per email. Opening it again adds nothing. Clicking a link in an email More than an open, once per link per email. Filling in a form More again: the contact raised their hand. Registering for an event, and attending The strongest signals. Missing an event they registered for Points taken off. Unsubscribing, or asking not to be contacted A large number of points taken off. A hard bounce (invalid email) The score drops to zero.

Sending or delivering an email gives no points: the contact did nothing yet.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Use the decay score to prioritise. Two contacts with the same engagement score are not equal if one engaged last week and the other last year.
  • Scores update every day. Today's activity shows tomorrow.
  • Companies are scored too, from the engagement of their contacts. See Companies.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Mailing lists
docs.text: Lists people subscribe to, such as your newsletter or a members' club, with their consent kept for each list.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text: A segment is a rule; a mailing list is a commitment. When someone joins a list, from a sign-up form or because you added them, they agreed to receive what that list sends. GoodBards keeps each person's status per list, so you always know who may receive what, and an unsubscribe is respected everywhere.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: • Contacts to add, or a form people can sign up with.

docs.title: How to manage a mailing list
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, choose Audience → Contacts, then the Mailing Lists tab. Each list shows its description and number of members.

  2. To create one, choose New Mailing List, then give it a name and a description.

  3. Click a list to open it. The counters show who is Subscribed, Pending, Unsubscribed, and Not on list.

  4. Below, each member shows their contact status, their status on this list, and how they joined. Revoke takes someone off the list.

  5. Embed Form gives you a sign-up form for your own website that adds people to this list.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Unsubscribed means locked. Someone who unsubscribed from a list cannot be added back, or removed, by anyone on your team. Only they can re-subscribe. This is how GoodBards keeps you compliant with PDPA and similar laws.
  • Lists do not update themselves. A segment re-evaluates its rule every time; a mailing list only changes when people join or leave. See Contacts.
  • Email the list from a campaign. When you send an email, choose the list as the audience. See Emails.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Content Hub
docs.text:
Write, store and reuse your content: articles, posts, press releases and the files behind them.

Who sees it: everyone your administrator gives the Content hub access to.

docs.title: Content Workspace
docs.text:
Write with an AI writer and reviewer. Give a short brief (topic, audience, format); the writer drafts it in your brand voice, the reviewer scores it and says what to improve, and you revise until it is ready to save.

See Content Workspace.

docs.title: Research & Plan
docs.text:
What to write next: topics your market searches for, questions your customers ask and gaps against competitors, each one ready to turn into a brief.

See Research & Plan.

docs.title: Content Repository
docs.text:
All your files and content in one place: documents, images, articles and posts, in folders, searchable by their content.

See Content Repository.

docs.title: Translator
docs.text:
Translate a text or a document while keeping its formatting.

See Translator.

docs.title: Content Workspace
docs.text: Write articles and posts with an AI writer and an AI reviewer: you give a short brief, the writer drafts in your brand voice, the reviewer scores it, and you revise until it is ready.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text: A blank page is slow, and a first AI draft is rarely publishable. The workspace splits the job: one AI writes, a second one reviews the draft against your brief and your brand, gives it a score out of 100 and says what to improve. You stay in charge of what gets saved.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: • Your brand voice set up, so the writer sounds like you. See How the AI knows your brand.

docs.title: How to write a piece
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, choose Content Hub → Content Workspace, then New Content. You can also start from a topic in Research & Plan, or from an action in Actions.
  2. Fill in the form: the topic, who it is for, the format (for example a LinkedIn post or a blog article) and the tone. Give the AI material to work from: notes, web pages (up to 3) and files from your Content Repository (up to 5). A link pasted in your notes is read like an imported page.
  3. Press Write it. Everything runs from here, one step after the other: your materials are read, a brief is written, the writer drafts the piece, the reviewer scores it, and the writer revises once if the score asks for it. About two minutes.
  4. Read the score and the reviewer's notes. Show the brief opens the brief the piece was written from, with the list of pages and files the AI could read (a page the site owner blocks is listed as blocked, not silently skipped). If the angle or the facts are off, edit the brief and press Write again from this brief.
  5. Not there yet? Ask for a revision in your own words, for example shorter, with a Singapore example. Each revision is scored again.
  6. When you are happy, save it. It goes to your Content Repository, ready to edit, schedule or post.

docs.title: Your briefs and pieces
docs.text: The Content Workspace lists every brief with the piece written from it, its format, its status and its score. Resume one where you left off, open the saved piece with Open Asset, or delete it.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• The score is a guide, not a gate. Press-ready means the reviewer found nothing important to fix; you can still save a lower score.
  • The writer uses your data. Started from Research & Plan, the brief already holds the searches and questions behind the topic.
  • Your materials reach every step. The pages, files and notes you give are read by the writer and by the reviewer, not only by the brief. A fact that is in one of your pages counts as a fact, not as something the AI made up.
  • Writing content for a whole campaign is different. From a campaign's dashboard, Write content with AI still shows you the brief before it writes several pieces at once, so you can check it before the batch runs.
  • Saving does not publish. A saved piece is a draft in the Content Repository until you post or send it.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Research & Plan
docs.text: What to write next, ranked from your own data: what your market searches for, the questions people ask AI assistants, and the gaps against your competitors.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text: Content that nobody searches for brings nobody. Research & Plan looks at your site, your Search Console data and your competitors, and ranks the topics most likely to bring visitors, each with its monthly searches and competition.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Google Search Console connected under Connections, for your own searches.
  • Your competitors listed under Brand & Context → Competitors.

docs.title: How to use it
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, choose Content Hub → Research & Plan.

  2. Read Recommended for you: each topic with why it is there (for example a gap against competitors), its monthly searches, its competition and its trend.

  3. Choose Add on a topic to put it on your list as To do, then write it in the Content Workspace.

  4. Have your own idea? Type it in the box at the top and choose Check Idea: it is checked against the same data and lands under Your ideas.

Refresh Plan ranks the topics again from the latest data. The language and market used, for example English · Global, are shown at the top right; choose them to change.

docs.title: The analysis behind the plan
docs.text:
From an idea, choose Explore demand trend to open the Analysis tools: four views of the data the plan is ranked from. Back To Plan returns.

Tab What it shows Demand Searches rising around your strongest term, including topics you have nothing for yet. Add To Queue turns one into an action. Topics Where your search traffic sits in the buying journey: Learning, Comparing or Ready to buy. Traffic piled at one end is worth knowing about. Content gaps Subjects your competitors write about and you do not rank for, scored on how worth covering they are for you. Signals Your own searches over the last four weeks against the four before: Gaining ground (moving up) and What people ask (questions in your searches).

Topics reads English wording

The buying-journey split looks for English words. On a site whose visitors search in another language, only part of the searches can be placed; the screen tells you how much.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Searches are a monthly average from Google; a small number in a niche market can still be worth it.
  • Low competition is the opportunity. A topic with steady searches and low competition is usually the quickest win.
  • Check your own idea before writing it. If nobody searches for it, the check says so before you spend the time.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Check-in and badges
docs.text: On the day: check guests in with their QR code, at the door or at a self-service kiosk, and print name badges.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text: A paper list at the door is slow and tells you nothing afterwards. Every confirmed guest of a GoodBards event has a personal QR code; scanning it checks them in in a second, and their attendance is recorded on their contact for the follow-up.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A phone, tablet or laptop with a camera.
  • Guests confirmed: only confirmed guests receive a QR code, in their confirmation email and in the event reminders.

docs.title: How to check guests in
docs.text:
Open the event and its Actions menu.

  • Scan attendee: for a host at the door. Point the camera at the guest's QR code and the guest is checked in.
  • Kiosk mode: for self-service. Put a tablet at the entrance; guests hold up their QR code and check themselves in. Choose Exit to leave kiosk mode.

A guest who lost their email can be found on the Attendance tab: search for their name and set their status to Attended.

docs.title: How to print badges
docs.text:
1. On the Attendance tab, under Badge, choose the Badge label format for your label printer, or keep your company's default.
  2. Line 1 is the guest's name. For line 2, pick the form field to print under it, for example their company.
  3. Choose Print Test Badge to check the layout, then print badges from the guests' rows.

docs.title: After the event
docs.text: Choose Actions → End event. Guests who were not checked in are marked Absent, so the Follow-up tab can thank those who came and reach those who missed it. Export attendees downloads the list.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• The QR code is personal. It checks in that one registration; a screenshot forwarded to a friend still checks in the original guest.
  • Pending and waitlisted guests have no QR code. They get one in the email that confirms their seat.
  • Check the camera before doors open. The browser asks for permission to use it the first time.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Ticket types and waitlist
docs.text: Offer several ticket types or time slots, each with its own number of seats, and decide what happens when the event is full.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text: Many events are not one block of seats: a workshop has paid seats and free observer places, a store opening runs in three time slots. Ticket types let each guest pick one, and each fills up on its own. When seats run out, the waitlist keeps the next people in line instead of turning them away.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: • An event. See Run an event from start to finish.

docs.title: How to set up ticket types
docs.text:
1. Open the event, then the Registration tab.
  2. Under Settings, set the Max Capacity for the whole event.
  3. Under Ticket types, turn on Use ticket types / time slots, then choose Add Ticket Type for each one: its name, its number of seats, and, for a time slot, its own start and end time.

On the registration form, each guest picks one ticket type. The guest's emails and badge show their own slot and time.

docs.title: How the waitlist works
docs.text:
1. Under Settings, turn on Waitlist.
  2. Choose how a freed seat is given:
    • Automatic: the next person in line gets it and is emailed straight away.
    • Manual: you choose. On Attendance, use ↑ Promote on a waiting guest. It only works when a seat is free.

With ticket types, each type has its own waitlist: a seat freed in one slot goes to someone waiting for that slot.

Guests on the waitlist receive the On the waitlist email; when they get a seat, the Spot opened email. See Registration emails.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• The overall capacity still applies. If the ticket types add up to more seats than the event's capacity, the event fills before every type does. The screen warns you when that happens.
  • Raising the capacity seats people. In Automatic mode, raising the capacity or a ticket type's seats moves the first people in line onto the list, and emails them.
  • Cancel with ⊘ to free a seat. Cancelling a registration with ⊘ offers the seat to the waitlist; changing a status from the status menu does not.

Still stuck? Contact support.

1. Go to live.goodbards.ai.
  2. Choose Sign Up.
  3. Sign up either with Google, or with your work email and a password.
  4. Verify your email address using the link sent to your inbox.

Already have an account?

Go straight to the login page. If you have forgotten your password, Forgot Password? below the password field sends you a reset link.

docs.title: Signing in
docs.text:
The login screen also carries three controls worth knowing about, along the top:

Control What it does SG Your region. EN Interface language. Sun / moon Switches between light and dark appearance.

You can change all three later from inside the app — see Personal Settings.

docs.title: What to set up first
docs.text:
A new workspace is empty. Four things make everything else work better, roughly in this order:

  1. Brand & Context — tell GoodBards what your company does. Everything the AI writes draws on this, so it is worth doing before generating any content.
  2. Brand Kit — your colours, fonts and logo, so emails and images come out on-brand automatically.
  3. Connections — link your social accounts and analytics. Most "why is there no data?" questions trace back to a missing connector.
  4. Contacts — import the people you market to. Without contacts there is nobody to send to.
  5. Your team — invite your colleagues and choose what each one can see and change. See Settings.

Do the brand setup before generating content

Agents use whatever is in Brand & Context at the moment they write. Filling it in afterwards does not improve drafts you have already produced.

docs.title: Then publish something
docs.text:

  • Launch a Tactic — one post on one channel, the quickest way to see the platform work end to end.
  • Send an email — design, preview and send to your contacts.

docs.title: What is GoodBards?
docs.text:
GoodBards is an Agentic AI Marketing OS — a single platform where AI agents plan, create and execute marketing campaigns, while remembering your brand's voice, data and history.

In practice that means the work you would normally spread across an email tool, a social scheduler, a CRM and a folder of brand assets happens in one place, with AI that already knows your business.

This documentation is a user guide: how to do things, screen by screen. For what GoodBards offers and why, see goodbards.com.

docs.title: Where each part of the product lives
docs.text:
If you arrived from the GoodBards website, you will have seen the platform described as a set of solutions. Inside the app those are grouped slightly differently — by the job you are doing rather than by what was sold. Here is how they line up.

On the website In the app Documentation Email Marketing Marketing → Emails Emails & Forms Customer Data Platform Audience Audience Social Media Marketing Social Media Social Media Event Management Marketing → Event Management Events SEO and AI search Organic Visibility Organic Visibility AI Chatbot and AI Agent Agentic AI, and Tool Box → External Chatbot Agentic AI

The docs follow the app, not the website

This documentation is organised the way the product's own sidebar is organised, so what you read matches what you click. If you are looking for something you saw on the website, the table above tells you where it lives.

Tactic — one piece of marketing on one channel: a single LinkedIn post, one email. The smallest thing you can publish.

Campaign — several tactics working towards one goal over a period of time.

docs.title: Create a social post from scratch
docs.text: Write one post yourself, by hand, save it as an asset, add it to a campaign and publish or schedule it. This is the quickest way to get a single post out when you already know what you want to say.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text: Not every post needs a brief or an article behind it. A quick announcement, a reminder of a deadline, a reply to something in the news: you type it, check it in the network's preview, and send it. The post is still saved as an asset in your Content Repository and still goes out through a campaign, so its results count with the rest.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A connected account for the network you post to: LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram, X or TikTok. See Connections. Without it, Publish and Schedule stay greyed out.
  • A campaign with a tactic for that network, to publish from. If you have none yet, you can create one as you go (step 3).

docs.title: 1. Create the asset
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, choose Social Media → Social Post, then New Post.

  2. In Create New Asset, leave Family on Social Media and pick the Asset Type: for example LinkedIn Post, Instagram Post (images), Instagram Reel (video) or Facebook Post. Use Filter by Tactic to show one network only.

  3. Choose Next.

  4. Under Creation Method, keep New Empty. (Write with AI drafts the post for you; Duplicate Existing copies one of your posts. Both are covered in Social Post.)

  5. Type a Title. It names the asset in your lists; it is not part of the post. Leave Marketing Stage and Folder as they are unless you sort your assets.

  6. Choose Create. The post editor opens.

docs.title: 2. Write the post
docs.text:
1. Type your text under Compose your Post. The counter shows how much of the network's limit you have used, and the preview on the right shows the post as it will appear, on Desktop or Mobile.
  2. Add hashtags under Hashtags: type one and press Enter. AI Hashtags suggests some once the post has ten words.

  3. Choose Image to attach a picture from your Content Repository, or Emoji to insert one. Improve With AI rewrites the post from an instruction (shorter, add a question at the end).

    On LinkedIn, Insert → Video… or Insert → Document (PDF, PowerPoint, Word)… attaches a video or a document instead of a picture. For an Instagram Reel, pick the video first. See Videos, documents, Reels and stories.

  4. Choose Save at the top right. In Save Document, check the title and choose Save again.

The message Asset created confirms it. Back on Social Post, your post is a card with View Tactics 0: it exists, but it is not attached to any campaign yet.

docs.title: 3. Add it to a campaign
docs.text:
1. On the post's card, choose View Tactics, then Add To Tactic.

  2. Keep Existing campaign, choose the campaign under Select campaign, then the tactic under Select tactic. Only tactics for the post's network are offered.

    No campaign for it yet? Choose New campaign instead, give it a name and a marketing objective, and choose Create & Launch.

  3. Choose Add To Tactic. The Tactics window now lists the campaign and tactic, with the post as Draft and two buttons on the row: Publish and Schedule.

docs.title: 4. Publish or schedule it
docs.text:
• Publish sends it now: choose the Destination (the page or account to post to) and confirm.

  • Schedule sends it later: pick a Date & Time, or choose Generate AI Recommendations for the best slots for your audience, then the Destination, then Confirm Schedule.

For Instagram, Publish as sets whether it goes out as a Post or a 24-hour Story.

The band on the post's card then reads Scheduled or Published with the date. A post with a video or a document shows Sending for a few minutes first, while the network processes the file. You can also do both from the campaign: open the tactic, and under Asset Management use the post's ⋮ menu.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Save before you leave the editor. The editor does not save on its own unless you switch Autosave on at the top. Leaving with Unsaved on the title loses the post.
  • One asset, one network. A LinkedIn post can only go to a LinkedIn tactic. For the same message on several networks, create one asset per network, or write them in one go with Write with AI or from an article: see Social Post.
  • Character limits are per network: 3,000 on LinkedIn, 280 on X, 2,200 on Instagram and TikTok. The counter turns red past the limit.
  • Instagram needs a picture or a video. A text-only Instagram post cannot be published.
  • Published posts are locked. You cannot edit or delete them from GoodBards once they are out.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Run an email marketing campaign
docs.text: Choose who to reach, write the email, send it from a campaign, and read what happened.

docs.title: What it's for
