Products & Services Each product or service with a description, its web page and keywords. The AI links to the right page and uses the right words. Press Release Information The CEO's name and title, your boilerplate in 25, 50 and 100 words, and the media contact. Used for every press release the AI drafts. Privacy Statements The statements contacts accept on your forms; one is the default. A statement is a text (any length, with bold, italic and bullet lists) or a link to a page on your site. See Adding contacts.

docs.title: Marketing Campaigns: campaign defaults
docs.text: Set once the values every new campaign starts from: marketing objective, budget, customer type, audience, regions and countries, target industry and campaign duration. The fields marked Visible to AI prefill new campaigns, so Create New Campaign opens already filled in. See Campaigns.

docs.title: Website: what GoodBards knows about your site
docs.text:
• Search Console property: which site the Organic Visibility screens read; change it under Connections.
  • What the site scan found: GoodBards reads your homepage and detects your site type (for example Online store), language and target market, with the evidence it used. Scan Again after a redesign.
  • Site type, language and market: keep the detected values or choose your own, then Apply. They decide which ideas rank highest in Research & Plan and Page Fixes, and the language content is written in. Reset To Detected goes back to the scan's values.

docs.title: Competitors
docs.text:
List the companies you compete with, and GoodBards analyses their websites.

  1. On the Competitors tab, choose Add Competitor and give its website.
  2. GoodBards scans the site. Open a competitor's Details for:
    • Overview: an AI summary, estimated domain authority, an SEO score and estimated monthly traffic, with their key strengths and weaknesses;
    • SEO Data, Content and Marketing: what they rank for, publish and promote.
  3. Tag competitors (for example furniture, online-first) with + Edit to keep the list readable.

Active competitors are given to your AI agents, and feed Research & Plan's content gaps. Figures marked AI Estimate are estimates, not measurements.

docs.title: Controlling what the AI can see
docs.text:
Every field carries a badge showing whether the AI can use it:

  • Visible to AI — the agent may use this when writing.
  • Hide From AI — choose this to keep a field out of AI-generated content.

Most details are safe and useful to share. Hide anything commercially sensitive that you would not want appearing in a draft.

Populate With AI

Populate With AI, at the top right, fills these fields in by reading your website. It is a fast way to start — but read what it produces before accepting it, since everything the AI writes later builds on it.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Do this before generating content. Agents use whatever is here at the time they write. Filling it in afterwards does not improve drafts already produced.
  • Be specific. "We help companies grow" tells the AI nothing. What you sell, to whom, and what makes you different is what gets used.
  • Revisit it. When your positioning changes, update this — otherwise the AI keeps writing last year's message.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Connections
docs.text: Link GoodBards to the outside services your marketing depends on — social accounts, analytics, storage and more.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
GoodBards can only publish to a social channel, or report on your website traffic, if you have given it permission to reach that account. A connector is that link.

Most "why can't I see any data?" problems come back to a missing connector, so this is worth setting up early.

docs.title: How to connect a service
docs.text:
1. Open your account menu (your picture, top right), then choose Connections.
  2. Pick the category across the top — for example Social Media or Web Analytics.
  3. Find the service and choose Connect.
  4. Sign in to that service and grant the permissions it asks for. You are taken back to GoodBards when it is done.

Use Search connectors… to find one by name rather than hunting the tabs.

docs.title: Categories
docs.text:
Each connector has its own page: what it lets GoodBards do, what you need before connecting, and what GoodBards reads or publishes. See All connectors.

Category What it connects Social Media LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram, Twitter (X), YouTube, TikTok. Instant Messenger Messaging platforms. Web Analytics Google Analytics, Search Console and similar. Digital Ads Advertising accounts. Storage External file storage. CRM Your customer relationship system. CMS Your website or content system. Email Email sending and mailbox services.

docs.title: Managing an existing connection
docs.text:
A connected service shows the account it is linked to, plus:

  • Manage Configuration — settings for that connector, such as which page or property to use by default.
  • Disconnect — removes the link. Anything relying on it stops working.

Connect the right account

The card shows which account is linked. On a shared channel, make sure it is the company account and not someone's personal profile — the person who connects it is the person whose access is used.

docs.title: Connectors your plan does not include
docs.text: Some connectors show a crown and a greyed-out Connect button. These are available on higher plans; speak to your account contact to enable them.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Connect before you build. Setting up a campaign for a channel you have not connected means going back and redoing the setup.
  • Connections can expire. If a service is failing, check here first — many providers require periodic re-authorisation.
  • Disconnecting is not retroactive. Already-published posts stay published; you simply cannot publish more until you reconnect.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Personal Settings
docs.text: Your own profile, password and preferences — the settings that affect you rather than your whole team.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text: Everything here is yours alone. Changing your language or your writing preferences does not affect colleagues, unlike AI Settings or Brand & Context.

docs.title: How to update your profile
docs.text:
1. Choose your profile picture at the top right, then Personal Settings.
  2. On Profile Information, update your details.

docs.title: Profile Information
docs.text: Field What it does Profile Image Your picture as colleagues see it. Full name Your name as it appears in the app. Role Your job title. Country Your country of residence. Custom Instruction Standing guidance for the AI when it writes for you.

docs.title: Custom Instruction is worth filling in
docs.text:
This is where you tell the AI how you like content written — for example a preference for bullet points over long paragraphs, or a particular tone. It applies whenever the AI generates something for you.

It is limited to 300 characters, so be specific rather than exhaustive.

Yours, not your company's

Custom Instruction is a personal preference. For how the AI should represent your brand, use the Voices Bank in Brand & Context.

docs.title: Password & Security
docs.text:
Change your password here, and turn on Two-Factor Authentication.

Turn on two-factor authentication

With 2FA enabled, signing in needs a verification code as well as your password. If your marketing account can email your entire contact database, it is worth protecting properly.

docs.title: Preferences
docs.text: Interface preferences, including your language. You can also switch language from the EN control in the top bar.

docs.title: My Memory
docs.text: What the AI has remembered about you and how you work. Review it if the AI's output drifts from what you expect.

docs.title: Shortcuts
docs.text:
Choose the icons shown in the top bar, before the search. Up to six pages or actions — for example Scan Business Card to capture a business card in one tap, or Emails if you send campaigns every day.

  1. Tick the entries you want. They are grouped like the menu, plus Quick actions (Create Contact, Scan Business Card, Create Campaign…).
  2. Use the arrows on each one at the top to set the order, left to right.
  3. Choose Update.

Reset to default brings back Content Repository and Calendar. Remove every entry and only the search is left.

Same shortcuts in every workspace

Your shortcuts follow you. A shortcut to a screen a workspace does not give you access to is simply not shown there; one your plan does not include shows a crown.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• These settings follow you, not the workspace. If you have access to more than one workspace, your personal settings apply across all of them.
  • Your name appears to colleagues. Fill it in properly if you work in a team.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Usage & Billing
docs.text: Track what your team has used against your plan, so nothing stops working unexpectedly.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
AI features consume credits. Generating copy, creating an image, running an agent — each uses some of your monthly allowance. This screen shows how much you have used and what has been driving it.

Worth checking monthly. Running out mid-campaign is avoidable if you can see it coming.

docs.title: How to check your usage
docs.text:
1. Open your account menu (your picture, top right), then choose Tenant Usage.
  2. Pick a period — 24h, 7d, 30d or 90d.

docs.title: What the numbers mean
docs.text:
Figure What it tells you Credits Used Your consumption in the selected period. Total Requests How many times an AI feature was called. Monthly Credit Quota The percentage of your monthly allowance used, with consumed and limit below. Daily Token Usage Day-by-day consumption, so you can see which days were heavy.

The Monthly Credit Quota dial is the one to watch. At 5% with three weeks to go you have plenty of room; at 80% with a week left, plan accordingly.

Tokens are a unit of AI text

Input tokens are what you send the AI, output tokens are what it returns. Longer prompts and longer responses both cost more. You do not need to manage tokens directly — the credit quota is the number that matters.

docs.title: The other tabs
docs.text:
Tab What it shows AI Overview The summary described above. AI Request Details Individual requests, useful for tracing a spike. Guardrails Your plan's limits and how much of each you use: monthly AI credits, messages per conversation, storage, users, API keys, sub-workspaces, posts published and emails sent this month, contacts and chat agents. Models Which AI models were used, and how much.

Check Guardrails before a big campaign: if a limit is close (for example emails sent this month), the send stops when it is reached.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Usage is shared across your team. The quota belongs to your company, not to each person, so a colleague's heavy week shows here too.
  • Check before a big campaign. Generating a large batch of content uses noticeably more than day-to-day work.
  • Investigate spikes. A sudden jump usually means a bulk generation job; AI Request Details will show what it was.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Sub-Workspaces
docs.text:
Run separate workspaces underneath your own — one per client, brand or business unit.

The app calls these sub tenants

You will see the word tenant on this screen. A tenant is simply a workspace — a self-contained account with its own data. This page uses "workspace", but the buttons say "tenant".

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
An agency running marketing for several clients does not want all that work in one pile. A sub-workspace is a self-contained space with its own contacts, campaigns and content, sitting under your main account.

Each has its own plan tier and its own credit allowance, so one client's heavy month does not consume another's.

If you run marketing for a single business, you will not need this.

docs.title: How to create a sub-workspace
docs.text:
1. Open your account menu (your picture, top right), then choose Tenant Settings.
  2. Open the Sub Tenants tab.
  3. Choose Create Sub Tenant.
  4. Give it a name and set its tier.

docs.title: Reading the list
docs.text:
Each row shows:

Column What it tells you Name The sub-workspace. Choose it to open. Tier Its plan — for example Pro. Users Who has access. Credit Usage Consumption against that workspace's own allowance.

The bar at the top right shows how many sub-workspaces you have against your limit — for example 1 / 5 tenants.

docs.title: Switching between workspaces
docs.text:
Use the workspace name at the top of the screen. Anything you then do — creating a campaign, adding contacts — happens inside the workspace you have selected.

Check which workspace you are in

The name at the top is the only thing distinguishing one from another. Before sending an email or publishing a post, confirm you are in the right workspace — content sent from the wrong one goes to the wrong audience.

docs.title: The other tabs
docs.text: Tab What it holds Preferences The workspace's name, timezone, engagement decay and badge format (below). Security Users, roles, contact ownership and API keys. See Users, roles & permissions. Sub Tenants The sub-workspaces described on this page.

docs.title: Preferences
docs.text:
• Organisation Name: the workspace name everyone sees in the top bar.
  • Timezone: the workspace's timezone, used for schedules and reports.
  • Engagement Decay Velocity: how fast old engagement stops counting in the decay score, for example 8 weeks (Normal). Shorter suits fast buying cycles, longer suits long B2B ones. See Lead scoring.
  • Attendee Badge Format: the default label size for event badges, with a preview and Print Test Badge. Badges under 80 mm wide print a compact layout. Each event can override it. See Check-in and badges.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Data does not leak between workspaces. Contacts and campaigns in one are invisible to another. This is deliberate — it is what makes the separation safe for client work.
  • Each has its own credits. Check usage per workspace rather than assuming a shared pool.
  • Your limit depends on your plan. The counter at the top right shows how many more you may create.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Users, roles & permissions
docs.text: Invite your colleagues and decide, module by module, what each one can see and change.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text: Not everyone in your company needs everything. A sales colleague needs the contacts, not the ad budget; an agency client may only need the reports. GoodBards gives access per module, each in read-only or read-and-write, and bundles those permissions into roles you give to people.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: • You need to be an administrator or the owner of your company account.

docs.title: The 12 modules
docs.text:
Access is given per module. They match the sections of the sidebar and of this documentation.

Module What it covers Home Home, the Daily Pulse, Actions, Calendar Audience Contacts, companies, segments, mailing lists Marketing Campaigns and tactics Emails and forms Emails, email designs, forms Events Event Management Social media Social posts and analysis Digital ads Digital Ads Content hub Content Workspace, Research & Plan, Content Repository, Translator Website and SEO Organic Visibility, Google Analytics, Google Trends AI studio Agentic AI Tool box QR codes, short links, chatbot, scheduler, image editor Settings Brand & Context, Brand Kit, connectors, AI settings

Each module is either read (see only) or write (see and change). A module someone has no access to disappears from their sidebar. Their own Personal Settings are always open to them.

docs.title: How to invite a user
docs.text:
1. Open Tenant Settings from your account menu, then the Security tab.
  2. Under Users, choose Invite User, enter their email and pick their role.
  3. They receive an invitation by email. The number of users your plan allows is shown above the list.

The invitation link stays valid for 7 days. Pending invitations are listed under Users until they are accepted, where you can extend or cancel them. If the email did not arrive, invite the same address again: the same link is sent again and its validity restarts. Someone who is already a member cannot be invited; change their role instead.

To change someone's role later, use the pencil next to their roles.

docs.title: The roles
docs.text:
Under Roles, the Platform roles are ready to use:

Role What they can do Tenant Owner Everything, plus billing and transferring ownership. Tenant Administrator Everything, plus users and company settings. Marketer Every module in read and write, and every contact. The usual role for your marketing team. Contacts' emails and phones stay hidden until you give them Access sensitive data. Sales Home and the Audience only, with Access sensitive data. With contact ownership on, they see only the contacts they own.

To give a group exactly the modules it needs, choose Create Role, name it, and pick the permissions. For example, a Reporting role with read access to Home, Marketing and Website and SEO, for a client who only follows results.

docs.title: Additional permissions
docs.text:
Three permissions are not tied to a module. They are given to a person, not to a role, and no role grants them except Sales, which includes Access sensitive data. A Marketer or an administrator does not have them until you tick them.

Permission What it gives Access sensitive data See contacts' email addresses, phone numbers and other personal details, and add or import contacts. Without it, these fields are hidden everywhere: lists, contact pages, exports and the assistant. Recipient for daily report emails Receive the Daily Pulse by email each morning: what changed, what needs attention, and the state of your connectors. Recipient for lead capture alert emails Receive an email each time your chatbot captures a new lead, with their details and a summary of the conversation.

To give one of them:

  1. Open Tenant Settings from your account menu, then the Security tab.
  2. Under Users, choose the pencil in the person's Permissions column (Edit permissions).
  3. Under Additional permissions, tick the ones they need, then choose Update Permissions.

The change applies at their next login, or when they switch workspace.

Nobody receives the emails until you choose who

If no one in your company has Recipient for daily report emails, the Daily Pulse email is not sent. If no one has Recipient for lead capture alert emails, new chatbot leads are still saved as contacts, but nobody is told. Give each to at least one person.

Keep sensitive data to the people who need it

Access sensitive data is what lets someone read and download personal details. Under Singapore's PDPA and similar laws, give it only to colleagues who work with contacts directly.

docs.title: Contact ownership
docs.text:
Each contact can have owners: the colleagues responsible for them. Turn on Restrict contacts to their owners to make people without the see every contact permission (the Sales role) see only the contacts and companies they own. Administrators and Marketers keep seeing everything.

Owners are assigned on the contacts list: select contacts, then Assign Owners. See Contacts.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Write includes read. Someone with write on a module can also see it.
  • Owners and administrators are never restricted. Their access cannot be reduced by a role.
  • Owners are recorded even when the restriction is off, so you can turn it on later without reassigning anyone.
  • API keys for connecting your own tools are on the same tab, below the roles. See Use the GoodBards API.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Connectors
docs.text:
Every service GoodBards can connect to, what each one gives you, and how to set it up.

To connect any of them, open your account menu (your picture, top right), then choose Connections. Only an administrator or the owner of your company account can connect or disconnect a service. See Connections for how the screen works.

docs.title: Social Media
docs.text: Connector What it gives you Page LinkedIn Publish to your company page; page analysis and reports. LinkedIn LinkedIn Community @mention people and companies in LinkedIn posts. LinkedIn Community Instagram Publish picture posts and carousels; account analysis and reports. Instagram Facebook Publish to your Page; Page analysis and reports. Facebook Twitter (X) Publish posts with pictures; account analysis. Twitter (X) Google Youtube Channel analysis (read-only). YouTube TikTok Publish videos. TikTok

docs.title: Instant Messenger
docs.text: Connector What it gives you Page Telegram Coming soon. — WhatsApp Coming soon. —

docs.title: Web Analytics
docs.text: Connector What it gives you Page Google Analytics Website traffic, conversions and revenue from GA4. Google Analytics Google Search Console Google search clicks, impressions, positions and queries — the base of the search screens. Google Search Console Google Trends Search interest over time and by place. Google Trends Chartbeat Stores your Chartbeat access; no screen shows its data yet. Chartbeat Google BigQuery Lets your AI agents read your own BigQuery data, in your Google project. Google BigQuery

docs.title: Digital Ads
docs.text: Connector What it gives you Page Google Ads Create, manage and report on campaigns; Keyword Planner. Google Ads

docs.title: Storage
docs.text: Connector What it gives you Page Google Drive Attach Drive files to agent conversations; sync a Drive folder. Google Drive

docs.title: CRM
docs.text: Connector What it gives you Page Pipedrive Import your Pipedrive people and organisations as contacts. Pipedrive

docs.title: CMS
docs.text: Connector What it gives you Page Wordpress (Self Hosted) Send blog posts as drafts; import your existing articles. WordPress (self-hosted) WordPress.com Send blog posts as drafts. WordPress.com

docs.title: Email
docs.text: Connector What it gives you Page Goodbards, Amazon-ses, Gmail, Sendgrid The server that delivers your email campaigns. Email sending

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• A crown means your plan does not include it. Speak to your account contact.
  • Connect with a shared, company-owned account where you can. The person who connects is the person whose access GoodBards uses.
  • Disconnecting never deletes what was already published or imported.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Chartbeat
docs.text: Link your Chartbeat account, for real-time audience data on your websites.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
Chartbeat measures, in real time, how readers use your site: top pages, referrers, where readers are, headline tests and conversions. The Chartbeat connector stores your Chartbeat key and the sites you want GoodBards to read.

No screen shows Chartbeat data yet

You can connect Chartbeat today. GoodBards screens do not display its data yet.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• You must be an administrator or the owner of your GoodBards company account.
  • You need a Chartbeat API key, from your Chartbeat account.
  • Know the hosts (site addresses) Chartbeat tracks for you, for example example.com.

docs.title: How to connect
docs.text:
1. Open your account menu (your picture, top right), then choose Connections.
  2. On the Web Analytics tab, find Chartbeat and choose Connect.
  3. Fill in the form:
    • API Key: your Chartbeat API key.
    • Hosts: the site to read. Use Add host to add more.
  4. Choose Save Settings. GoodBards checks each host with Chartbeat before saving.

To change the key or the hosts later, choose Edit Configuration on the card. Test this host checks a saved host again.

docs.title: What GoodBards does with it
docs.text: GoodBards… Details Reads Real-time and historical figures for your hosts: top pages, quick stats, referrers, locations, headline tests and conversions. Does not Change anything in Chartbeat.

docs.title: How to disconnect
docs.text:
1. On the Chartbeat card, choose Edit Configuration.
  2. Choose Disconnect.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Email sending
docs.text: Choose how your marketing emails are sent: through GoodBards, or through your own Amazon SES, Gmail or SendGrid account.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
Before GoodBards can send an email campaign, it needs an email server: the service that actually delivers your messages, from your own address. Without one, sending fails. See Emails.

The Email tab of Connections offers four:

Server Choose it when… Goodbards You want GoodBards to deliver for you, from your own domain. Nothing to sign up for. Amazon-ses Your company already sends through its own Amazon SES account. Gmail You send small volumes from a Gmail or Google Workspace address. Sendgrid Your company already has a SendGrid account.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• You must be an administrator or the owner of your GoodBards company account.
  • Know the sender name, sender address and reply-to address your emails should use.
  • For Goodbards, you need someone who can add DNS records to your domain (often your IT team or web agency).

docs.title: How to connect
docs.text:
1. Open your account menu (your picture, top right), then choose Connections.
  2. Open the Email tab.
  3. Choose the server's card, then Connect. Its settings open.
  4. Fill in the fields for that server (below), plus the three sender fields: Sender Name, Sender Address and Reply To Address.
  5. Save. The card shows a green tick once connected.

docs.title: Goodbards
docs.text:
• Email Domain: your domain only, for example mycompany.com — not an email address.
  • Choose Show DNS Records and add every record listed to your domain's DNS:
    • a TXT record that proves you own the domain;
    • three CNAME records (DKIM) that sign your emails;
    • a TXT record for DMARC.

Until those records are in place, mail from your domain cannot be delivered reliably. DNS changes can take a few hours to take effect.

docs.title: Amazon-ses
docs.text:
• AWS Access Key ID and AWS Access Key Secret: a key from your AWS account that is allowed to send with SES.
  • AWS Region: the region where your SES is set up.
  • Email Domain: the domain verified in your SES.

docs.title: Gmail
docs.text:
• Gmail Address: the address you send from.
  • App Password: a Google app password, not your normal password. The settings panel links to Google's help on creating one.
  • SMTP Host and SMTP Port: for Gmail, smtp.gmail.com.

docs.title: Sendgrid
docs.text: • API Key: a SendGrid API key that can send mail.

docs.title: Test before you send
docs.text: In the server's settings, choose Test Config, enter an Email Address, then Send Test Email. Check that it arrives — and not in spam.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Use an address on your own domain. With Goodbards, a sender address that is not on your domain (or one of its sub-domains) is replaced by your default sender.
  • Your plan sets a monthly sending allowance. See Usage & Billing.
  • Servers your plan does not include show a crown.

docs.title: How to disconnect
docs.text:
1. On the Email tab, open the connected server's settings.
  2. Choose Disconnect.

Emails can no longer be sent through that server until you connect one again.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Facebook
docs.text: Publish posts to your Facebook Page and get reports on how it performs.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
The Facebook connector links GoodBards to one of your Facebook Pages. With it you can:

  • Publish and schedule posts from a campaign's social tactic. See Launch a tactic and Social Post.
  • Link a post you published outside GoodBards, so its results count in the campaign report.
  • Analyse your Page: followers, post results and comments. See Social Media Analysis and Reports.
  • Schedule recurring reports with the Scheduler.
  • Feed the daily summary on your home page.
  • Let your AI agents list your Pages and read or create analysis reports.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• You must be an administrator or the owner of your GoodBards company account.
  • Use a Facebook profile that manages the Page you want to publish to.

docs.title: How to connect
docs.text:
1. Open your account menu (your picture, top right), then choose Connections.
  2. On the Social Media tab, find Facebook and choose Connect.
  3. Sign in to Facebook. When Facebook asks which Pages GoodBards may use, select the Pages you want — Pages you leave out will not appear in GoodBards.
  4. Back in GoodBards, choose Manage configuration on the Facebook card.
  5. Under Destination (one per tenant), pick your Page, then choose Save configuration.

If the list is empty, reconnect and make sure you select your Pages in step 3.

docs.title: What GoodBards does with it
docs.text: GoodBards… Details Publishes Posts on the chosen Page: text, text with a link preview, or text with one or several pictures. Deletes A published post, when you remove it from GoodBards. Reads Your Pages, their fans and followers, posts, post statistics, comments and daily Page statistics. Does not Publish videos, reels or stories, or read your messages.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• One Page per workspace. The Page you pick is used for publishing and for the automated reports.
  • Picture or link preview, not both. Without a picture, the first link in the text becomes a preview card.
  • Some figures are no longer available. Facebook no longer provides impressions or reach for every post through its API.
  • Access expires. When Facebook's access runs out, the connector switches off and you need to connect again.

docs.title: How to disconnect
docs.text:
1. On the Facebook card, choose Manage configuration.
  2. Choose Disconnect, then confirm.

GoodBards forgets the access and the chosen Page. Posts already published stay on Facebook. To remove GoodBards' access on Facebook's side too, do it from your Facebook settings, under business integrations.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Google Ads
docs.text: Run and report on your Google Ads campaigns from GoodBards.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
The Google Ads connector links one Google Ads account to your workspace. GoodBards uses it in:

  • Digital Ads: overview, campaigns, ad groups, keywords, ads, recommendations, conversion tracking and callouts. See Digital Ads.
  • Ad campaign tactics: link a campaign tactic to an existing Google Ads campaign and follow its results in the campaign report.
  • Keyword Planner: keyword ideas with monthly searches, competition and bids — in the campaign wizard, when you write content, and as a demand source in Research & Plan.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• You must be an administrator or the owner of your GoodBards company account.
  • Use a Google account with access to the Google Ads account you want to use. To create and change campaigns from GoodBards, that access must allow changes, not read-only.
  • Agencies with a manager account (MCC): sign in with the account that has access to the manager. GoodBards lists each client account under it.

docs.title: How to connect
docs.text:
1. Open your account menu (your picture, top right), then choose Connections.
  2. On the Digital Ads tab, find Google Ads and choose Connect.
  3. Pick your Google account and allow GoodBards to manage your Google Ads campaigns.
  4. Back in GoodBards, choose Manage Configuration on the card.
  5. Under Google Ads Account, pick the account, then choose Save Settings.

In the list, accounts reached through a manager show via MCC and the manager's number; test accounts show TEST. Manager accounts themselves cannot be picked: they do not run ads, so pick one of their client accounts.

Until an account is chosen, Digital Ads shows Select a Google Ads account.

docs.title: What GoodBards does with it
docs.text:
GoodBards reads and changes your Google Ads account.

GoodBards… Details Reads Accounts, campaigns, ad groups, keywords, ads, conversion actions, callouts, recommendations, reports and keyword ideas. Creates and changes Campaigns and their budgets, status and bidding; ad groups, keywords, negative keywords and ads; conversion actions; callouts. Applies or dismisses Google's keyword recommendations, when you choose to.

docs.title: Safety rules
docs.text:
• New campaigns start paused. Nothing spends until you enable it.
  • Google checks every change first. The campaign wizard only lets you create once Google has validated the campaign.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• One account per workspace. All Google Ads screens and reports use the account you picked.
  • Changes apply at once in Google Ads. Removing a campaign is permanent there.
  • Keyword Planner answers are kept for 30 days, so asking again for the same keywords is instant.
  • Ad text limits follow Google's: up to 15 headlines of 30 characters, up to 4 descriptions of 90 characters, and callouts of 25 characters.

docs.title: How to disconnect
docs.text:
1. On the Google Ads card, choose Manage Configuration.
  2. Choose Disconnect.

GoodBards forgets the access and the chosen account. Your campaigns keep running in Google Ads exactly as they are — pause them in Google Ads if you need to. To remove access on Google's side too, do it from your Google Account, under third-party connections.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Google Analytics
docs.text: Bring your website traffic and conversions from Google Analytics 4 into GoodBards.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
The Google Analytics connector reads your GA4 property. GoodBards uses it in:

  • Organic Visibility → Google Analytics: visits, traffic sources, top pages, countries and AI insights. See Google Analytics.
  • Performance & Report: the business outcomes (conversions, revenue, sessions). See Performance & Report.
  • Momentum: page views per page. Without Google Analytics, Momentum falls back on Search Console data. See Momentum.
  • Page Fixes: pages that convert are given higher priority. See Page Fixes.
  • Digital Ads: your converting pages, as a signal when you write ads. See Digital Ads.
  • The daily summary on your home page.
  • AI agents with the Google Analytics tool, which can run reports for you. See Chat agents.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• You must be an administrator or the owner of your GoodBards company account.
  • You need a Google Analytics 4 property. Older Universal Analytics properties are not supported.
  • Use a Google account that can view that property.

docs.title: How to connect
docs.text:
1. Open your account menu (your picture, top right), then choose Connections.
  2. On the Web Analytics tab, find Google Analytics and choose Connect.
  3. Pick your Google account and allow GoodBards to see your Google Analytics data.
  4. Back in GoodBards, choose Manage Configuration on the card.
  5. Under GA4 Property, pick the property for your website, then choose Save Settings.

Until a property is chosen, the Google Analytics screens have nothing to show.

docs.title: What GoodBards does with it
docs.text: GoodBards… Details Reads Your accounts and properties, and reports on visits, users, sessions, page views, events, conversions, transactions and revenue, including real-time figures. Does not Change anything in Google Analytics.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• One property per workspace. Every Google Analytics screen and report uses the property you picked.
  • Recent days may be incomplete. GA4 is still processing the latest data.
  • Revenue is in your GA4 currency.

docs.title: How to disconnect
docs.text:
1. On the Google Analytics card, choose Manage Configuration.
  2. Choose Disconnect.

GoodBards forgets the access and the chosen property. To remove access on Google's side too, do it from your Google Account, under third-party connections.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Google BigQuery
docs.text: Let GoodBards read your own BigQuery data, so your AI agents can answer questions from your warehouse.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
If your company keeps its data in Google BigQuery (website events, sales, subscriptions), the Google BigQuery connector lets GoodBards read it. Your data stays in your Google project: GoodBards runs read-only queries there and copies nothing.

Set up with your data team

Connecting needs a key file that only someone with access to your Google Cloud project can create. The steps below tell them exactly what to do. Once you have the file, the GoodBards side takes two minutes.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• You must be an administrator or the owner of your GoodBards company account.
  • Ask your data team for a service-account key file (a .json file). Send them this checklist:
    1. In the Google Cloud project that holds the data, create a service account named for GoodBards.
    2. Give it BigQuery Data Viewer on each dataset GoodBards may read, and BigQuery Job User on the project.
    3. Create a JSON key for that service account and send you the file.
  • Queries are billed to that Google Cloud project, at BigQuery's usual rates. A cap limits what one query may scan (1 GB unless you change it).

docs.title: How to connect
docs.text:
1. Open your account menu (your picture, top right), then choose Connections.
  2. On the Web Analytics tab, find Google BigQuery and choose Connect.
  3. Choose Choose file and pick the key file, or paste its content in the box below. GoodBards shows the account it found in the file.
  4. GCP project is filled in from the file. Change it only if your data team told you to.
  5. Choose Save & connect. GoodBards checks the key with Google and lists the datasets it can see before saving. If Google refuses, nothing is saved and the message tells you why.

The card then shows the service account and the project. Manage configuration opens the same form; Test connection lists the datasets again at any time.

docs.title: What GoodBards does with it
docs.text: GoodBards… Details Reads Only the datasets your data team granted. Queries are read-only and run in your project. Stores The key file, encrypted. It is never shown again, not even to administrators. Does not Change anything in BigQuery, copy your tables, or read datasets the account was not granted.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Under Advanced, you can raise or lower the per-query cost cap. Leave it unless your data team asks for more.
  • To rotate the key, open Manage configuration, choose Replace key, pick the new file and save. The old key stops being used immediately.
  • Some companies block the creation of service-account keys by policy. If your data team cannot create one, contact support before going further.

docs.title: How to disconnect
docs.text:
1. On the Google BigQuery card, choose Manage configuration.
  2. Choose Disconnect. The stored key is deleted.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Google Drive
docs.text: Use files from your Google Drive in GoodBards.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
The Google Drive connector lets you bring Drive files into GoodBards:

  • Attach Drive files to an AI agent conversation. In the agent chat, open the attachments menu and choose Google Drive. Google's own file picker opens: select one or several files, including from shared drives. See Chat agents.
  • Keep a Drive folder in sync with your Content Repository, with a Drive sync task in the Scheduler.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• You must be an administrator or the owner of your GoodBards company account to connect it.
  • Use the Google account that holds, or has access to, the files.

docs.title: How to connect
docs.text:
1. Open your account menu (your picture, top right), then choose Connections.
  2. On the Storage tab, find Google Drive and choose Connect.
  3. Pick your Google account and accept the permissions.
  4. You are taken back to GoodBards. The card shows the account name.

Until it is connected, the agent chat shows Google Drive (Not connected).

docs.title: How to sync a Drive folder
docs.text:
1. Open the Scheduler and create a task of type Drive sync.
  2. Fill in:
    • Google Drive folder ID: the last part of the folder's address in Drive.
    • Google Drive folder name (optional).
    • The destination folder in your Content Repository.
  3. Choose how often it runs, then save.

docs.title: What GoodBards does with it
docs.text: GoodBards… Details Reads The files you pick, and the files of the folder you sync. Converts Google Docs, Slides and Drawings into PDF, and Google Sheets into Excel, when it brings them in. Does not Create, change or delete anything in your Drive.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Folders cannot be picked in the agent chat — pick the files inside.
  • GoodBards only sees what you give it through Google's file picker. If a synced folder seems to miss files, open the picker and select those files once: Google then lets GoodBards read them.
  • Imported files are copies. Changing the file in Drive later does not change the copy in GoodBards, unless a Drive sync task brings it in again.

docs.title: How to disconnect
docs.text:
1. On the Google Drive card, choose Disconnect.
  2. Confirm.

Files already brought into GoodBards stay there. To remove access on Google's side too, do it from your Google Account, under third-party connections.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Google Search Console
docs.text: Bring your Google search results — clicks, impressions, positions and queries — into GoodBards.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
The Google Search Console connector is the main source for GoodBards' search screens:

  • Performance & Report: clicks, impressions, position and click rate, alerts, page inspection and Diagnostics. See Performance & Report.
  • Page Fixes: the pages to fix first. See Page Fixes.
  • AI Readiness & Authority. See AI Readiness.
  • Momentum: which pages are gaining or losing search traffic. See Momentum.
  • Research & Plan: a plan needs Search Console connected and a site chosen. See Research & Plan.
  • Digital Ads: your top search queries, and the Search Console source when you choose keywords. See Digital Ads.
  • The daily summary on your home page.
  • AI agents with the Search Console tool.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• You must be an administrator or the owner of your GoodBards company account.
  • Your website must be a verified property in Google Search Console, and the Google account you use must have access to it.

docs.title: How to connect
docs.text:
1. Open your account menu (your picture, top right), then choose Connections.
  2. On the Web Analytics tab, find Google Search Console and choose Connect.
  3. Pick your Google account and allow GoodBards to view your Search Console data.
  4. Back in GoodBards, choose Manage Configuration on the card.
  5. Under Search Console Site, pick your website, then choose Save Settings.

docs.title: What GoodBards does with it
docs.text: GoodBards… Details Reads Your sites, search results by date, query, page, device and country, page inspection results and your sitemaps. Does not Change anything in Search Console.

docs.title: Changing the site
docs.text:
Picking a different site is not a simple switch. GoodBards asks you to confirm first (Change your Search Console site?), because:

  • unfinished actions queued for the old site are closed, and the dialog tells you how many;
  • what GoodBards learned from the old site — its content plans, Momentum moves, reports and its detected site type — no longer applies.

Choose Keep current site if you are not sure.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• One site per workspace. Every search screen uses the site you picked.
  • Data is two to three days behind. That is how Google provides it.
  • Page inspections are limited by Google to 2,000 a day per site.

docs.title: How to disconnect
docs.text:
1. On the Google Search Console card, choose Manage Configuration.
  2. Choose Disconnect.

GoodBards forgets the access and the chosen site. To remove access on Google's side too, do it from your Google Account, under third-party connections.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Google Trends
docs.text: See how much people search for a topic, over time and by place.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
The Google Trends connector reads Google's search-interest data. GoodBards uses it in:

  • Organic Visibility → Google Trends: compare search terms over time and by location. See Google Trends.
  • Research & Plan: the demand signals behind a content plan. See Research & Plan.
  • AI agents with the Google Trends tool.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• You must be an administrator or the owner of your GoodBards company account.
  • You need a Google account.

docs.title: How to connect
docs.text:
1. Open your account menu (your picture, top right), then choose Connections.
  2. On the Web Analytics tab, find Google Trends and choose Connect.
  3. Pick your Google account and accept the permissions, including access to search trends.
  4. You are taken back to GoodBards. The card shows the account name.

docs.title: What GoodBards does with it
docs.text: GoodBards… Details Reads Search interest over time (by day, week, month or year) and by country, region, sub-region or city. Does not Change anything in your Google account.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Not every place has a sub-region breakdown. Google does not provide one for every location.
  • Recent days may be incomplete. Google's latest figures are still settling.

docs.title: How to disconnect
docs.text:
1. On the Google Trends card, choose Disconnect.
  2. Confirm.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Instagram
docs.text: Publish picture posts, carousels, Reels and stories to your Instagram account and get reports on how it performs.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
The Instagram connector links GoodBards to your Instagram account. With it you can:

  • Publish and schedule posts from a campaign's social tactic. See Launch a tactic and Social Post.
  • Link a post you published outside GoodBards, so its results count in the campaign report.
  • Analyse your account: followers, reach, post results and comments. See Social Media Analysis and Reports.
  • Schedule recurring reports with the Scheduler.
  • Feed the daily summary on your home page.
  • Let your AI agents read or create analysis reports.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• You must be an administrator or the owner of your GoodBards company account.
  • Use an Instagram professional account (Business or Creator). You sign in with Instagram directly, not through Facebook.

docs.title: How to connect
docs.text:
1. Open your account menu (your picture, top right), then choose Connections.
  2. On the Social Media tab, find Instagram and choose Connect.
  3. Sign in to Instagram with the account you want to publish to, and accept the permissions it asks for: your profile, publishing, comments, messages and statistics.
  4. You are taken back to GoodBards. The card shows the account name.

docs.title: What GoodBards does with it
docs.text: GoodBards… Details Publishes A picture post (one picture), a carousel (2 to 10 pictures) or a Reel (one video, also shown in your grid), with your caption. Any of them can go out as a 24-hour story instead. Reads Your profile, followers, posts, post statistics, daily reach and views, post comments, and the numbers of the stories published from GoodBards. Does not Mix pictures and videos in a carousel, add stickers to stories, read stories posted directly in the Instagram app, delete posts, or read your messages.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Every Instagram post needs a picture or a video. A text-only post fails.
  • Videos are published as Reels: MP4 or MOV, up to 300 MB, 3 seconds to 15 minutes. A video story: up to 100 MB and 60 seconds. See Videos, documents, Reels and stories.
  • Pictures are sent as JPEG, whatever their original format.
  • 2,200 characters per caption.
  • Media become reachable by link. Instagram fetches pictures and videos itself, so GoodBards gives it a link to each one: pictures stay publicly reachable, videos through a link that expires after an hour.
  • Instagram limits how many posts you can publish per day (about 50 per account).
  • Access is renewed automatically a week before it expires. If Instagram refuses, the connector switches off and the card asks you to reconnect.

docs.title: How to disconnect
docs.text:
1. On the Instagram card, choose Manage configuration.
  2. Choose Disconnect, then confirm.

GoodBards forgets the access. Posts already published stay on Instagram. To remove GoodBards' access on Instagram's side too, do it from your Instagram settings, under apps and websites.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: LinkedIn Community
docs.text: Tag people and companies with an @mention in the LinkedIn posts you write in GoodBards.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
A mention puts your post in front of the person or company you tag. This connector adds a Mention button to the post editor when you write for LinkedIn. You search for a person or a company page and GoodBards inserts the mention in your text.

It does not publish. Publishing and analytics go through the main LinkedIn connector, so connect that one too.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• You must be an administrator or the owner of your GoodBards company account.
  • Use a LinkedIn profile that has a role on your company page. The organisation you choose is used to search for people.

docs.title: How to connect
docs.text:
1. Open your account menu (your picture, top right), then choose Connections.
  2. On the Social Media tab, find LinkedIn Community and choose Connect.
  3. Sign in to LinkedIn and accept the permissions it asks for.
  4. Back in GoodBards, choose Manage configuration on the card.
  5. Under Destination (one per tenant), pick your company page, then choose Save configuration.

docs.title: How to mention someone
docs.text:
1. Write a LinkedIn post in the post editor. See Social Post.
  2. Choose Mention.
  3. Search for a person or a company, then pick them.

The mention is added to your text and becomes a real LinkedIn mention when the post is published.

docs.title: What GoodBards does with it
docs.text: GoodBards… Details Reads People and company pages matching your search, and your organisations with their logos. Does not Publish, delete or read the statistics of posts.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• The Mention button appears only once this connector is connected, and only when you write for LinkedIn.
  • Access is renewed automatically. If LinkedIn refuses to renew it, the card asks you to reconnect.

docs.title: How to disconnect
docs.text:
1. On the LinkedIn Community card, choose Manage configuration.
  2. Choose Disconnect, then confirm.

The Mention button disappears from the editor. Mentions already published stay on LinkedIn.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: LinkedIn
docs.text: Publish posts to your LinkedIn company page and get reports on how it performs.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
The LinkedIn connector lets GoodBards act on LinkedIn for you. With it you can:

  • Publish and schedule posts from a campaign's social tactic. See Launch a tactic and Social Post.
  • Link a post you published outside GoodBards, so its results count in the campaign report.
  • Analyse your company page: followers, post results, comments and who your audience is. See Social Media Analysis and Reports.
  • Feed the daily summary on your home page with your page's latest figures.
  • Let your AI agents list your pages and read or create analysis reports.

Want to @mention people and companies in your posts? That is a separate connector: LinkedIn Community.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• You must be an administrator or the owner of your GoodBards company account. Other roles see the Connect button greyed out.
  • Use a LinkedIn profile that has administrative access to your company page. The pages you can choose from are the ones this profile has an approved role on.
  • Plan to publish to a company page. A personal profile can publish, but it gives no analytics.

docs.title: How to connect
docs.text:
1. Open your account menu (your picture, top right), then choose Connections.
  2. On the Social Media tab, find LinkedIn and choose Connect.
  3. Sign in to LinkedIn and accept the permissions it asks for: your basic profile, posting on your behalf and on behalf of your pages, and reading your pages' posts, followers and statistics.
  4. Back in GoodBards, choose Manage configuration on the LinkedIn card.
  5. Under Destination (one per tenant), pick your company page.
  6. Choose Save configuration.

The card then shows the profile you connected with and, in italics, the page you publish on behalf of.

docs.title: What GoodBards does with it
docs.text: GoodBards… Details Publishes Public posts on the chosen page: text, a link preview, one or several pictures, a video, or a document (PDF, PowerPoint or Word) people swipe through. Reads Your pages, follower numbers, post statistics, follower demographics (seniority, industry, job function, location, company size) and post comments. Does not Delete or edit posts on LinkedIn, or post as anyone other than the chosen destination.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• One destination per workspace. The page you pick is used for publishing and for the automated reports.
  • Personal profiles have no analytics. If the destination is your personal profile, the daily summary skips LinkedIn and asks you to select a company page.
  • 3,000 characters per post, and up to 20 pictures.
  • One kind of media per post: pictures, one video or one document. Without any, the first link in the text becomes a preview card.
  • Videos: MP4 only, 75 KB to 500 MB, 3 seconds to 30 minutes. Documents: up to 100 MB and 300 pages; a PDF with one slide per page is how you post a carousel. See Videos, documents, Reels and stories.
  • Bold and italic are kept: GoodBards converts them into characters LinkedIn can display.
  • Access is renewed automatically. The card shows how long access is valid. If LinkedIn refuses to renew it, the connector switches off and the card asks you to reconnect.

docs.title: How to disconnect
docs.text:
1. On the LinkedIn card, choose Manage configuration.
  2. Choose Disconnect, then confirm.

GoodBards forgets the access and the chosen page. Posts already published stay on LinkedIn. To remove GoodBards' access on LinkedIn's side too, do it from your LinkedIn account settings.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Pipedrive
docs.text: Bring the people and organisations from your Pipedrive CRM into your GoodBards contacts.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text: If your sales team works in Pipedrive, the Pipedrive connector saves you re-typing contacts. Once connected, the Import Pipedrive Contacts page brings your Pipedrive people, then your organisations, into Contacts.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• You must be an administrator or the owner of your GoodBards company account.
  • You need two things from Pipedrive:
    • your company name as it appears in your Pipedrive address — the yourcompany in yourcompany.pipedrive.com;
    • your personal API token, from your Pipedrive personal preferences.
  • Decide which privacy statement and status imported contacts should get. See Adding contacts.

docs.title: How to connect
docs.text:
1. Open your account menu (your picture, top right), then choose Connections.
  2. On the CRM tab, find Pipedrive and choose Connect.
  3. Fill in:
    • Tenant Name: your Pipedrive company name.
    • Access Token: your Pipedrive API token.
  4. Choose Save Settings. The card shows your Pipedrive user name.

docs.title: How to import your contacts
docs.text:
In Audience → Contacts → Import Jobs, choose Bulk Add Contacts → From Pipedrive. On Import Pipedrive Contacts, fill in:

Field What it does Title A name for this import. Choose Conflict Action Ignore keeps existing contacts as they are; Overwrite updates them from Pipedrive. Default Status The status imported contacts get. Only subscribed contacts receive emails. Tags Tags added to every imported contact. Privacy Statement The statement the contacts agreed to. Your company default is filled in. Notes A note added to each contact.

Choose Upload to start. Every imported contact gets the referral source Pipedrive Contacts Import. The import runs in the background.

docs.title: What GoodBards does with it
docs.text: GoodBards… Details Reads Your Pipedrive people and organisations, and your own Pipedrive user. Does not Write anything back to Pipedrive, or read deals.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• It is a one-off import, not a live sync. Run it again to pick up new people.
  • Import only people who agreed to hear from you. Choose the status with care.

docs.title: How to disconnect
docs.text:
1. On the Pipedrive card, choose Disconnect.
  2. Confirm.

Contacts already imported stay in GoodBards.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: TikTok
docs.text: Send videos and photo posts to your TikTok account from a campaign.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
The TikTok connector lets GoodBards prepare TikTok posts for you:

  • Send TikTok videos and photo posts from a campaign's social tactic, now or at a scheduled time. They arrive in your TikTok inbox as drafts; you finish and post them in the TikTok app. See Launch a tactic and Social Post.
  • Track the posted video in the campaign, like any other published post.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• You must be an administrator or the owner of your GoodBards company account.
  • Have your video in the Drive (Drive → New → Video), in portrait (9:16) format, or your photos in the Drive.

docs.title: How to connect
docs.text:
1. Open your account menu (your picture, top right), then choose Connections.
  2. On the Social Media tab, find TikTok and choose Connect.
  3. Sign in to TikTok and accept the permissions it asks for: your profile and statistics, your videos, sending videos to your TikTok inbox, and publishing videos. Keep every box ticked.
  4. You are taken back to GoodBards. The card shows your TikTok name and picture, a View profile link, and until when the access is valid.

If you unticked a permission, the card shows Permissions missing — reconnect in amber. Hover it to see which ones, then choose Reconnect and keep all the boxes ticked.

docs.title: Two kinds of TikTok post
docs.text:
When you create the asset, choose its type:

Type What it holds TikTok Video One video from the Drive: MP4, MOV or WebM, up to 10 minutes and 4 GB, at least 360 pixels. The text is the caption. TikTok Photos (carousel) Up to 35 photos from the Drive. The main photo is the cover, the asset title is the post title (90 characters) and the text is the description (4,000 characters).

docs.title: How a post reaches TikTok
docs.text:
1. In the campaign, choose Publish (or Schedule) on the TikTok asset.
  2. GoodBards sends it to your TikTok inbox as a draft. In the campaign table it shows Published with an In TikTok inbox tag.
  3. Open the TikTok app, open the draft from your inbox notification, finish it (sound, effects, who can see it) and post it.
  4. Back in GoodBards, open the asset's menu and choose Check TikTok post. GoodBards links the video, and its numbers appear in the campaign report. If TikTok does not say which video it became (a private post), choose Pick the posted video and select it in the list.

docs.title: Posting directly (when available)
docs.text:
Where direct posting is switched on, Publish on a TikTok asset offers Post now on TikTok or Send to TikTok inbox. Posting now shows TikTok's own posting screen:

  • Who can view this post: choose one; there is no default.
  • Allow users to comment, duet or stitch: off until you tick them, and greyed out when they are turned off in your TikTok settings.
  • Disclose post content: turn it on when the post promotes your own business (Your brand, labelled "Promotional content") or another brand (Branded content, labelled "Paid partnership"). Branded content cannot be private.
  • The caption is editable, and posting means agreeing to TikTok's Music Usage Confirmation (and Branded Content Policy when it applies).

The post then appears on your profile after TikTok has processed it, which can take a few minutes. In the campaign it shows Processing on TikTok until you use Check TikTok post. Scheduled posts always go to the inbox.

docs.title: What GoodBards does with it
docs.text: GoodBards… Details Sends Your video, or your photos with their title and description, to your TikTok inbox as a draft. You post it yourself in the app. Reads Your profile and your videos' views, likes, comments and shares. Does not Post without you, or delete videos.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• A video draft arrives without its caption. TikTok does not take the text with a video draft. In the editor, choose Copy caption and paste it in TikTok when you post. Photo posts keep their title and description.
  • 5 drafts at a time. TikTok keeps at most 5 drafts waiting in your inbox over 24 hours. Post or delete the waiting ones before you send more.
  • Scheduled posts arrive as drafts too. At the scheduled time the draft lands in your inbox; someone still has to post it.
  • You can link a video you posted yourself. Use Link published post on the TikTok tactic and paste the video's link (tiktok.com/@your-account/video/…) or pick it in the list.
  • Access is renewed automatically for one year from the day you connect. The card shows the date; connect again before it. If TikTok refuses earlier, the connector switches off and you need to connect again.
  • Connect from your own session. The TikTok sign-in must be finished within 10 minutes, by the same person, in the same company account that started it.

docs.title: How to disconnect
docs.text:
1. On the TikTok card, choose Disconnect.
  2. Confirm.

GoodBards forgets the access. Videos already posted, and drafts waiting in your inbox, stay on TikTok.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Twitter (X)
docs.text: Publish posts to your X account and get reports on how they perform.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
The Twitter (X) connector links GoodBards to your X account. With it you can:

  • Publish and schedule posts from a campaign's social tactic. See Launch a tactic and Social Post.
  • Analyse your account: profile figures and the results of your latest posts. See Social Media Analysis.
  • Feed the daily summary on your home page.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• You must be an administrator or the owner of your GoodBards company account.
  • Sign in to X in your browser with the account you want to publish to before you start.

docs.title: How to connect
docs.text:
1. Open your account menu (your picture, top right), then choose Connections.
  2. On the Social Media tab, find Twitter (X) and choose Connect.
  3. Sign in to X and authorise GoodBards.
  4. Back in GoodBards, choose Manage configuration on the card.
  5. Under Select accounts to use, tick the account, then choose Save configuration.

docs.title: What GoodBards does with it
docs.text: GoodBards… Details Publishes Posts with text and pictures. Deletes A published post, when you remove it from GoodBards. Reads Your profile figures and your latest 20 posts (replies left out): likes, reposts, replies, bookmarks, quotes and views. Does not Publish videos.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• 280 characters per post, counted after links are shortened. Up to 4 pictures.
  • Links are checked. A post with a link that cannot be reached is refused.
  • Detailed statistics are for recent posts. Figures such as profile clicks are only available for posts less than 30 days old.

docs.title: How to disconnect
docs.text:
1. On the Twitter (X) card, choose Manage configuration.
  2. Choose Disconnect, then confirm.

GoodBards forgets the access. Posts already published stay on X. To remove GoodBards' access on X's side too, do it from your X settings, under connected apps.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: WordPress.com
docs.text: Link a blog hosted on WordPress.com.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
Use this connector if your blog is hosted by WordPress.com. If you run WordPress on your own hosting, use WordPress (self-hosted) instead.

Once connected, your WordPress.com site is offered as a destination in a campaign's Blog Post tactic. See Launch a tactic.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• You must be an administrator or the owner of your GoodBards company account.
  • Use a WordPress.com account that can write posts on the site.

docs.title: How to connect
docs.text:
1. Open your account menu (your picture, top right), then choose Connections.
  2. On the CMS tab, find WordPress.com and choose Connect.
  3. Sign in to WordPress.com and approve GoodBards.
  4. You are taken back to GoodBards. The card shows your site's name.

docs.title: What GoodBards does with it
docs.text: GoodBards… Details Creates A draft post with your title and content, with your picture as the featured image. Does not Publish the post for you — review and publish it in WordPress.com.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text: • Import WordPress in the Content Repository works with self-hosted WordPress only.

docs.title: How to disconnect
docs.text:
1. On the WordPress.com card, choose Disconnect.
  2. Confirm.

Drafts already sent stay on WordPress.com.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: WordPress (self-hosted)
docs.text: Send your blog posts to your own WordPress website, and bring your existing articles into GoodBards.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
Use this connector if your website runs on WordPress that you or your agency host (not on WordPress.com — for that, see WordPress.com). With it you can:

  • Send blog posts to WordPress from a campaign's Blog Post tactic. See Launch a tactic.
  • Import your existing articles into the Content Repository with + New → Import WordPress, so the AI can learn from what you already published. See Content Repository.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• You must be an administrator or the owner of your GoodBards company account.
  • You need a WordPress user that can write posts and upload media.
  • Create an Application Password for that user in WordPress: in your WordPress admin, open Users → Profile, then Application Passwords. It is not your normal login password.
  • Your site's WordPress REST API must be reachable (at https://yoursite.com/wp-json). Some security plugins switch it off.

docs.title: How to connect
docs.text:
1. Open your account menu (your picture, top right), then choose Connections.
  2. On the CMS tab, find Wordpress (Self Hosted) and choose Connect.
  3. Fill in:
    • Website URL: your site's address, for example https://yoursite.com.
    • Username: the WordPress user name.
    • Application Password: the application password you created.
  4. Choose Save Settings.

docs.title: What GoodBards does with it
docs.text: GoodBards… Details Creates A draft post with your title and content. The first picture is uploaded and becomes the featured image. Deletes The post, when you remove it from GoodBards. Uploaded pictures stay in your media library. Reads Your existing posts (for the import) and the post types you can publish to.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Posts arrive as drafts. Review them in WordPress and publish from there.
  • Pick the post type as destination. When you publish, GoodBards lists the post types your site offers.

docs.title: How to disconnect
docs.text:
1. On the Wordpress (Self Hosted) card, choose Disconnect.
  2. Confirm.

Drafts already sent stay in WordPress. You can also revoke the application password in WordPress.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: YouTube
docs.text: Bring your YouTube channel's results into GoodBards.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
The Google Youtube connector reads your channel's statistics so you can see them beside the rest of your marketing:

  • Analyse your channel: views, watch time, likes, comments, shares, impressions and click rate for your recent videos. See Social Media Analysis.
  • Feed the daily summary on your home page.

It is read-only: GoodBards does not upload or publish videos to YouTube.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• You must be an administrator or the owner of your GoodBards company account.
  • Use the Google account that owns the channel, or that is a manager of the Brand Account the channel belongs to.

Channels shared in YouTube Studio do not appear

If someone gave you access to a channel only through YouTube Studio permissions, Google does not let other apps read it. Ask for manager access to the Brand Account instead.

docs.title: How to connect
docs.text:
1. Open your account menu (your picture, top right), then choose Connections.
  2. On the Social Media tab, find Google Youtube and choose Connect.
  3. Pick your Google account. If Google asks, choose the channel or Brand Account you want to connect.
  4. Accept the permissions: view your YouTube account and view its analytics reports.

docs.title: What GoodBards does with it
docs.text: GoodBards… Details Reads Your channel, its videos, their public counters and their analytics (views, watch time, engagement, impressions and click rate). Does not Upload, publish, edit or delete videos.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Last 90 days. A report covers videos from the last 90 days, up to 200 videos.
  • Figures lag about two days. Until YouTube's analytics catch up, GoodBards shows the public counters.
  • Impressions take a few days to appear. The first time you connect, YouTube starts preparing impression reports for your channel. They start arriving after about two days, then fill in up to 30 days back.

docs.title: How to disconnect
docs.text:
1. On the Google Youtube card, choose Disconnect.
  2. Confirm.

GoodBards forgets the access. To remove it on Google's side too, do it from your Google Account, under third-party connections.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Social Media
docs.text:
Publish to your social channels and see how those posts performed.

Who sees it: everyone your administrator gives the Social media access to.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: Social publishing needs the channel connected first. See Connections: without it, there is nowhere for a post to go.

docs.title: Social Post
docs.text:
Write a post for LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook or X, with the AI's help for the text and hashtags, then publish it now or schedule it. You can also turn an article into a series of posts.

See Social Post.

docs.title: Analysis
docs.text:
How your social content performs across channels: reach, engagement and followers, post by post.

See Analysis.

docs.title: Social reports
docs.text:
Period reports per network (LinkedIn, Instagram, YouTube), sent to you on a schedule if you want.

See Social reports.

docs.title: Analysis
docs.text: See how your social content performed — reach, engagement, and how people reacted to it.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text:
Posting is only half the job. This is where you find out whether anyone saw a post, whether they engaged with it, and whether the reaction was positive.

Use it to decide what to do more of. A post with high impressions but almost no clicks tells you something different from one with few impressions and strong engagement.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
Your social account must be connected — see Connections.

LinkedIn organisation pages only

Report generation and analysis currently support LinkedIn organisation pages. Personal LinkedIn accounts are not supported, and the other channel tabs may have no report available yet.

docs.title: How to review social performance
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, choose Social Media → Analysis.
  2. Pick a channel from the tabs across the top.
  3. Choose which organisation page to report on.
  4. Use the arrows beside the date to move between reporting days.

Choose Change beside the organisation name to switch to a different page.

docs.title: What the numbers mean
docs.text:
Metric What it counts What to read into it Impressions How many times your content was shown. Reach. Low impressions mean a distribution problem, not a content problem. Engagement Rate The share of people who interacted. The single most useful number here — it is reach-independent. Likes Straightforward approval. Easy to earn, weak signal. Comments People who wrote something. Far stronger than a like: it costs effort. Shares People who passed it on. The strongest signal of all. Clicks People who followed your link. The one that matters when the post has a destination.

Judge posts on engagement rate rather than raw likes. A post seen by 500 people with 50 interactions is doing better than one seen by 30,000 with 100.

Facebook pages

Impressions, clicks and the Channel Engagements chart come from Facebook's insights, which the page connection has to allow. When it does not, those figures are left out of the report rather than shown as zero. Likes, comments, shares and Fans are always available. Reconnect the page to add insights access.

docs.title: Content Sentiment Analysis
docs.text:
Beside the metrics, sentiment splits engagement into Positive, Neutral and Negative.

This is worth watching over time rather than per post. A shift towards negative sentiment is worth investigating early — it is easier to address a small complaint than a pattern.

docs.title: Who your audience is (LinkedIn)
docs.text:
Audience Demographics breaks down the people who follow your LinkedIn page by Role, Seniority, Industry and Company Size. Check that it matches who you sell to: a B2B brand followed mostly by students has a reach problem, not a content problem.

Next to it, Channel Engagements shows the account's daily activity over the period, straight from the network: engagement (split by type on LinkedIn) and impressions.

docs.title: Top Posts Performance
docs.text: Below the summary, your best-performing content is listed with its engagement figures. This is the fastest route to understanding what your audience responds to: look for what the top posts have in common — format, topic, tone, time of day.

docs.title: Stories (Instagram)
docs.text:
Instagram reports have a Stories card for the stories published from GoodBards: views, reach, replies and how people moved through them. A story still showing on Instagram is marked Live, with a link to open it; its numbers are refreshed every 2 hours. After 24 hours the story disappears from Instagram, its numbers are captured one last time and marked Final.

Stories posted directly in the Instagram app are not listed: Instagram does not let GoodBards read them.

docs.title: TikTok
docs.text:
The TikTok tab shows the connected account: followers, following, likes received and number of videos, then your videos from the last 90 days with their views, likes, comments and shares.

TikTok gives no day-by-day statistics, so GoodBards takes a snapshot of the account every night and works out what changed:

  • Views, likes, comments, shares for the period are what your videos gained between snapshots, and the Channel Engagements chart shows them day by day.
  • Net followers is the change in followers over the period (it can be negative).
  • Numbers start the day after you connect TikTok. The first snapshot is the starting point, so the first days of a new connection show no gains.
  • Engagement rate on TikTok is likes, comments and shares per view.

If you unticked the statistics permission when connecting, the follower and likes counters are missing: reconnect TikTok and keep every box ticked.

docs.title: History
docs.text: History, at the top right, holds previous reports so you can compare periods rather than judging a single day in isolation.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• One day is not a trend. Social performance is noisy. Compare across several reports before changing your approach.
  • Impressions depend on the platform. Reach is decided by each network's algorithm, so a drop is not necessarily about your content.
  • Match the metric to the goal. For awareness, watch impressions; for traffic, watch clicks; for community, watch comments and shares.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Social reports
docs.text: A report per social account and period, kept in a history so you can compare weeks, and sent to you on a schedule if you want.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text: Network figures change every day. A report freezes them for a period: what was posted, how it did, and what people said. Kept week after week, the reports show the trend; sent automatically, they save someone collecting the figures by hand for the Monday meeting or for a client.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: • The social account connected under Connections. See Connections.

docs.title: How to read past reports
docs.text:
1. In the sidebar, choose Social Media → Analysis, then the network's tab, for example LinkedIn.

  2. Choose History at the top right. Each line is one report, with its date, status and what it covers.

  3. Choose the eye icon to open a report. The Analysis screen then shows that period.

To make a report now, for example after a big campaign week, choose Generate New Report. It takes about a minute.

docs.title: How to receive reports automatically
docs.text:
1. Choose Tool Box → Scheduler, then New Task.
  2. Pick Social report as the task type, then the account.
  3. Set how often, for example every Monday at 9:00, and who receives it.

See Scheduler.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• One report per account. A company with a LinkedIn page and an Instagram account gets two reports.
  • Channel-level figures are for the whole account. Tag filters on the Analysis screen apply to posts, not to those account-wide totals.
  • Deleting a report only removes it from the history. The posts and the network's own figures are not affected.

Still stuck? Contact support.

docs.title: Social Post
docs.text: Write social posts with AI or from your articles, attach them to a campaign, then publish or schedule them to your connected accounts.

docs.title: What it's for
docs.text: A social post usually starts from something you already have, a blog article or a press release, or from a short idea. GoodBards drafts the post for each channel, checks it against the channel's limits and your brand, and publishes it from the campaign it belongs to, so its results show up in the campaign report.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A connected account. Connect LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram, X or TikTok under Connectors (in the menu behind your avatar), and choose the page to publish to in Destination. Without it, Publish and Schedule stay greyed out.
  • A campaign with a social tactic, to publish from.

docs.title: How to create posts from an article
docs.text:
Turn one article into a series of posts for several channels at once.

  1. In the sidebar, choose Content Hub → Content Repository.
  2. On the article, open the ⋮ menu and choose Create social posts.
  3. Under Campaign, choose the campaign the posts belong to, then Next.
